title: Molten‐Salt Surface Restructuring of 3D‐Printed Agitator Exposes Ni0 Active Sites for Efficient Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Three‐dimensional (3D) printing enables the integration of structural engineering with catalytic functionality, yet extending this concept to high‐pressure liquid‐phase hydrogenation remains challenging because catalytic efficiency, selectivity, and structural robustness are difficult to optimize simultaneously. Here, we report a strategy that couples additive manufacturing with molten‐salt activation to engineer a 3D‐printed bladed agitator catalyst (AB–MSL–H
                    2
                    ). Molten‐salt treatment selectively reconstructs the alloy surface while preserving the printed architecture, generating a Ni‐enriched interface with abundant exposed metallic Ni
                    0
                    active sites. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that surface reconstruction enriches accessible Ni
                    0
                    sites to direct the desired hydrogenation pathway while suppressing isomerization, cyclization, and hydrogenolysis, whereas the integrated bladed architecture simultaneously enhances gas‐liquid‐solid mass transfer and reactant accessibility. Consequently, AB–MSL–H
                    2
                    achieves complete conversion of 2‐butyne‐1,4‐diol with a 1,4‐butanediol yield exceeding 97%. This work establishes a general strategy for transforming additively manufactured structural alloys into catalytically active reactor components through molten‐salt‐induced surface reconstruction, expanding the scope of catalyst‐reactor integration for high‐pressure liquid‐phase catalysis.

title: Indirect Characterization of 14N Nuclei via 1H‐Detected Rotating‐Frame Relaxometry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    14
                    N NMR is notoriously difficult to perform in liquids due to the very fast spin relaxation and the large quadrupolar couplings, which render many signals invisible. We show here how
                    14
                    N nuclei of biomolecular constituents can be probed indirectly by reintroducing the scalar relaxation of the second kind contribution as a relaxation pathway for J‐coupled protons in double resonance spin‐locking experiments. The enhanced
                    1
                    H relaxation rates in the rotating‐frame allow for direct evaluation of nitrogen chemical shifts and polarization lifetimes, from which one‐ and even two‐bond
                    1
                    H‐
                    14
                    N scalar couplings as well as
                    14
                    N quadrupolar interactions can be determined. We demonstrate the versatility of this method by characterizing
                    1
                    H‐
                    14
                    N spin pairs in several molecules of biological importance, showing proton relaxation enhancements beyond one order of magnitude. We further observe a pronounced effect from intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Our approach can be readily integrated into existing liquid‐state NMR methodologies, as demonstrated here for
                    1
                    H‐detected relaxation‐editing experiments with water suppression. This method provides access to nitrogen's picosecond‐modulated quadrupolar interaction via sensitive proton detection in systems that would otherwise yield almost no detectable direct
                    14
                    N signal even after averaging over thousands of transients.

title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I
                    2
                    ) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole‐transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine‐trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium‐based interfacial modifiers, PTZ‐PEFAI and PXZ‐PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy‐level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I
                    2
                    through halogen bonding, enabling I
                    2
                    capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I
                    3
                    −
                    in modifier‐iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine‐vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p‐type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy‐level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ‐PEFAI‐treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a
                    T
                    85
                    lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial iodine chemistry and charge transport toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Atomic‐Scale Origin of Charge Density Wave–Driven Metal–Semiconductor Transition in an Incommensurately Modulated Metal–Organic Framework
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Although metal–organic frameworks are widely recognized for their long‐range crystalline periodicity, they can also exhibit intrinsic aperiodic structures associated with incommensurate modulation, whose observation has been exceptionally rare. In low‐dimensional condensed matter physics, these unique structures often give rise to novel physical phenomena such as charge density wave. However, owing to limited direct experimental evidence, the relationship between incommensurate structural modulation and temperature‐dependent electronic transport in conductive metal–organic frameworks remains incompletely understood. Here, using high‐quality Pr
                    3
                    HHTP
                    2
                    (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) single crystals as a model system, we resolve the incommensurately modulated structure at 100 K (modulation vector
                    q
                     = 0.39143(12)
                    c
                    *
                    ) via temperature‐dependent single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction. The observed reversible metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K occurs in a similar temperature range to the disappearance of the structural modulation, supporting a connection between lattice distortion and electronic behavior. The modulation reappears upon cooling, with guest water molecules influencing both the extent of its recovery and the electrical conductivity of the material. This work establishes a concrete experimental criterion for one‐dimensional charge density wave in metal‐organic frameworks and provides an ideal platform for probing coupled electronic–lattice modulations.

title: Precisely Recyclable, Multifunctional, and High‐Performance Polyester Integrated by a Single Imidazolium‐Monomer
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sustainable lifecycle management of polymer materials urgently requires integrating green synthesis, service‐stage desired properties, and end‐of‐life easy recyclability. Herein, by introducing a single imidazolium‐monomer, the all‐in‐one integration of green preparation (without solvents or additives), multifunctionality (flame retardancy and antistatic property), high performance (excellent chromaticity, high heat resistance and high strength), and precise recyclability (in mixed wastes) for polyesters is achieved, which also reduces the health risks caused by additive migration. The key is that the imidazolium unit can not only control the C(alkyl)─O cleavage at high temperature to hinder polyester combustion but also catalyze the C(carbonyl)─O cleavage at the ester site to achieve chemical recycling of polyester. Without halogen or phosphorus elements, the polyester exhibits excellent chromaticity (L* value > 89 and b* value < 7), high glass‐transition temperature (75°C), increased strength (78.8 MPa), antistatic function (surface resistivity as low as 6 × 10
                    11
                    Ω), flame retardancy (the best UL‐94 V‐0 rating) and precise recycling in extremely complex mixed polymer wastes. This work successfully achieves lifecycle management of polyester materials via a single imidazolium‐monomer, providing a feasible platform for the next generation of sustainable, multifunctional and high‐performance polymer materials.

title: Biomimetic N‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Homologation is a key tactic used in the lead optimization of small‐molecule pharmaceuticals due to the potent impact such modifications can have on target affinity and physicochemical properties. However, while many elegant homologation strategies have been developed for the synthesis of β
                    3
                    ‐amino acids via decarboxylation, preparation of the β
                    2
                    ‐amino acid homologues remains underexplored. We report a general biomimetic strategy for the
                    N
                    ‐terminal homologation of amino acids using photoredox catalysis. Key to the success of this approach is a radical translocation cascade driven by single‐electron transfer. This methodology provides streamlined access to a range of cyclic and acyclic β
                    2
                    ‐amino acids and phosphonates, providing new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.

title: Interfacial Molecular Engineering Mediated Intramolecular Inter‐Group Relay Effect Enables Efficient Acidic CO2‐to‐C2+ Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrochemical CO
                    2
                    reduction reaction (CO
                    2
                    RR) in acidic media represents an attractive strategy for improving carbon utilization efficiency by suppressing carbonate formation. However, achieving highly selective C
                    2+
                    products at high current densities remains a formidable challenge due to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and sluggish C─C coupling process. Here, we introduce the surface‐adsorbed bifunctional organic molecule on Cu (Cu─SBMA), which delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 90.4% for C
                    2+

                    2+

                    ) moiety mediates protonation of *CO toward *CHO. The intramolecular inter‐group relay effect facilitates C─C coupling and suppresses HER. Our findings provide novel insights for the precise design of catalysts to regulate the reaction selectivity of complex multi‐step energy conversion process.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    It is challenging to understand how noncoordinating lattice guests regulate Mn
                    2+
                    luminescence without changing the metal coordination environment. Herein, we report a solvent‐removal‐induced single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal (SCSC) transformation from ethanol‐containing (C

As a result, the emission undergoes a distinct green (518 nm) to yellow‐green (543 nm) shift. Combined low‐temperature excitation spectroscopy, crystal‐field analysis, electron‐phonon coupling evaluation, and excited‐state decay kinetics establish a correlation between supramolecular lattice reconstruction, local ligand‐field modulation, and excited‐state relaxation. title: Dual‐DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi‐DUB Engagement
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Targeted protein stabilization has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring the abundance and function of disease‐relevant proteins. Deubiquitinase‐targeting chimeras (DUBTACs) offer a chemical approach to protein stabilization by recruiting deubiquitinases (DUBs) to promote target deubiquitination. However, current DUBTAC strategies generally rely on the recruitment of a single DUB, leaving the potential of engaging multiple DUBs through a common recruiter largely unexplored. Here, we report a dual‐DUBTAC strategy that enables targeted protein stabilization through the recruitment of two distinct DUBs. Using Degrasyn, a small‐molecule reversible covalent inhibitor of multiple DUBs, as a privileged scaffold, we engineered small molecules that selectively stabilize CFTR and cGAS and demonstrate that these compounds enhance target protein homeostasis through USP9X‐ and USP5‐mediated deubiquitination in cells. By decoupling substrate stabilization from reliance on a single DUB, the Dual‐DUB platform confers adaptability across diverse ubiquitin chain architectures and rewired proteostasis networks characteristic of heterogeneous tumors and could overcome potential drug resistance in future clinical applications. This strategy expands the chemical space for restoring protective proteins and establishes a general framework for functional reactivation of destabilized tumor‐suppressive pathways.

title: Cryptochiral Circularly Polarized Luminescence Emerges From Cosolvent‐Regulated Pathway Complexity in Amyloidogenic Peptide Self‐Assembly
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is important for chiral photonics, optical encryption, bioimaging, and information processing. It is usually associated with an identifiable chiral ground‐state organization, and CPL without detectable ground‐state chirality remains comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report a rare “
                    cryptochiral CPL
                    ” phenomenon arising from cosolvent‐regulated pathway complexity in the self‐assembly of a naphthalimide (NMI)‐amyloidogenic peptide conjugate (PEP‐L). In water, PEP‐L spontaneously forms thermodynamically stable, emissive nanofibers with pronounced supramolecular chirality and strong CPL. Adding a small amount of cosolvent redirects assembly toward kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies and shows no detectable Circular Dichroism (CD) response in the naphthalimide chromophore region, but retains pronounced CPL, which decouples ground‐state and excited‐state chiroptical responses. We term this behavior
                    cryptochiral CPL
                    . Thermal annealing or aging converts the spheres into thermodynamically favored nanofibers with distinct CD and CPL characteristics. The enantiomer PEP‐D shows mirror‐image chiroptical responses, which validates the phenomenon. Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under different conditions give molecular‐level insight into the conformation, noncovalent interactions, and supramolecular organization of the different assembly states. These findings establish a new conceptual framework for adaptive chiral photonic materials and open opportunities for hidden optical encoding and biomolecular photonic systems.

title: Entropy‐Compensated Electrolyte Enables Low‐Temperature 400 Wh Kg−1 Silicon‐Based Lithium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrolytes dictate the low‐temperature (LT) performance of Si‐anode lithium‐ion batteries, wherein bulk solvation governs Li
                    +
                    transport and interfacial stability. Especially, enlarged ionic clusters and strengthened ion pairing at LT hinder Li
                    +
                    migration, limiting Li
                    +
                    supply to the interface and destabilizing interfacial reactions. Herein, we propose an entropy‐compensation strategy to counteract LT‐induced solvation deterioration in Si‐anode electrolytes. Increasing the solvation entropy (
                    ΔS
                    solv
                    ) compensates for the LT‐induced increase in the Gibbs free‐energy change for ion‐cluster dissociation (
                    ΔG
                    solv
                    ), thereby raising the corresponding equilibrium constant (
                    K
                    solv
                    ) and suppressing ion pairing. Consequently, electrolytes preferentially form smaller anion‐rich ionic clusters, delivering an approximately threefold increase in ionic conductivity at −20°C. Enhanced bulk transport alleviates concentration polarization, stabilizes the interfacial solvation environment, and promotes uniform SEI‐forming reactions. Benefiting from this coupled bulk‐interfacial optimization, Ah‐level pouch cells retain 97.8% capacity after 165 cycles at −20°C and support sustained discharge at −81°C. This strategy enables high‐energy pouch cells to deliver 400 Wh kg
                    −1
                    under ambient conditions and 339 Wh kg
                    −1
                    at LT, while an Ah‐level pouch cell retains 80% capacity after 1150 cycles at 2 C. This work identifies
                    ΔS
                    solv
                    as a critical thermodynamic descriptor for low‐temperature electrolyte design.

title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe
                    2
                    nanoclusters onto MoSe
                    2
                    piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal‐support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long‐lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d‐band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g
                    −1
                    with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe
                    2
                    . Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g
                    −1
                    with stable long‐term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H2 Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H
                    2
                    evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni
                    SA
                    ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H
                    2
                    evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ
                    +
                    ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial
                    d‐p
                    orbital hybridization between Ni
                    SA
                    and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni
                    SA
                    cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni
                    SA
                    ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H
                    2
                    evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h
                    −1
                    g
                    −1
                    . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high‐performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

title: Photoreduction of Chlorinated Volatile Waste Into C2+ Hydrocarbons
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Chlorinated volatile organic compounds (Cl─VOCs) are a class of major environmental pollutants and potential human carcinogens. Dechlorination of Cl─VOC waste into harmless and value‐added chemicals under mild conditions is highly desirable yet challenging, and cannot be achieved using current photocatalytic methods. Here, we report the synthesis of the first nickel anthraquinone–thiolate complex for photoreduction of a variety of Cl─VOCs into unsaturated C
                    2+
                    hydrocarbons in good yields using visible light. Notably, the molecular system is capable of both reducing C
                    2
                    Cl─VOCs with high chlorine content into acetylene and C─C coupling of C
                    1
                    Cl─VOCs into ethylene and propylene. Mechanistic studies reveal that multielectron and multi‐proton reduction of the nickel complex is critical in generating the catalytically active species for various reductive dechlorination transformations. This study provides a blueprint for the conversion of chlorinated waste into highly valuable chemicals using solar energy.

title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less‐colored states upon heating due to disruption of π‐conjugation. In contrast, heat‐triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation‐switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone‐functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li
                    +
                    , Na
                    +
                    , and Ag
                    +
                    ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible‐ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li
                    +
                    /PF
                    6
                    −
                    ion‐pair‐cooperation‐promoted ring‐opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal‐ion‐regulated conjugation‐switching strategy for heat‐activated colorless‐to‐colored switching and responsive optical materials.

title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ether‐oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether‐oxygen groups into high‐connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]‐connected 3D COFs with
                    scu
                    topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight‐connected ether‐oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high‐stability light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether‐oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni‐incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2‐aminobenzenethiol to produce 2‐phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas‐phase H
                    2
                    product (∼1.15 mmol g
                    −1
                     h
                    −1
                    ). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale‐up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

title: Advancing C3 Polymerization of Alkynylcyclopropanes via a Synergistic Lewis Acid/Brønsted Base/C(sp3)–H Bond System
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The integration of cyclopropane chemistry with polymer science could offer access to unique all‐carbon polymers. However, the ring‐opening polymerization (ROP) of cyclopropanes generally requires strong electron‐donating and ‐withdrawing substituents, limiting the use of electronically less activated monomers such as 2‐alkynylcyclopropane‐1,1‐dicarboxylates (ACPs). Here, we demonstrate that the synergistic combination of a Lewis acid and a Brønsted base overcomes the electronic limitations imposed by carbon–carbon triple bonds, including their high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability, enabling the unprecedented C3 ROP of ACPs. This process is regulated by a reversible‐deactivation equilibrium mediated by chain‐end C(sp
                    3
                    )─H bonds, affording well‐defined polymers bearing alkyne side groups. The resulting functional polymers provide a versatile platform for applications ranging from stimulus‐responsive sensing to Raman imaging.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF
                    4
                    −
                    /─NH
                    2
                    +
                    ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH
                    2
                    ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The protolignin standardization transformation into high‐value‐added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3‐alkyl guaiacol (C3‐G), stoichiometric diazotization‐reductive ammonification of C3‐G to aminophenol C3‐GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3‐GAP to the benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor‐selective cytotoxicity of the as‐synthesized G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3‐GLB‐pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high‐value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    )‐derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO
                    2
                    ‐based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequences. Here, we introduce terpolymerization of CO
                    2
                    with cyclosilanes and epoxides to access poly(silyl ether–ester) with perfectly alternating A‐B‐C (CO
                    2
                    ‐
                    alt
                    ‐cyclosilane‐
                    alt
                    ‐epoxide) sequences. This terpolymerization is enabled by the thermodynamically favored formation of Si─O bonds, providing a driving force for efficient incorporation of both silalactones and epoxides into the terpolymer backbone in an alternating fashion. A range of epoxide and silacyclobutane substrates can be incorporated into the polyester, affording structurally diverse terpolymers. Notably, these polymers are stable thermally (
                    T
                    d
                    up to 313°C) and hydrolytically (in neutral water) but can slowly degrade under acidic or basic conditions and be chemically depolymerized under mild catalytic conditions to recover the silalactone monomer.

title: Radical Buffering by Isolated Ru and Fe Sites in ZSM‐5 for Selective Methane Oxidation to Formic Acid
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The selective conversion of methane under mild conditions is limited by the uncontrolled reactivity of radical intermediates (·CH
                    3
                    , ·OH) generated during Fe‐catalyzed oxidation with H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    . Here we report a radical buffering strategy in which atomically dispersed Ru is co‐loaded with Fe in ZSM‐5 as an ·OH reservoir, steering intermediates toward selective Eley‐Rideal‐type coupling in the micropores. The Ru‐Fe/ZSM‐5 catalyst achieves an oxygenate productivity of 37.5 mmol·g
                    cat
                    −1
                    ·h
                    −1
                    at 70°C with 95.7% oxygenate selectivity and 92.3% formic acid selectivity among liquid products, a 2.2‐fold improvement over Fe/ZSM‐5. Extended X‐ray absorption fine structure analysis shows that Ru and Fe exist as two independent populations of single atoms with no metal–metal bonding. Electron paramagnetic resonance and in situ infrared spectroscopy show that Fe activates CH
                    4
                    to ·CH
                    3
                    while Ru activates H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    and holds part of the resulting ·OH. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that Ru binds ·OH more strongly than Fe (−3.130 compared to −2.738 eV), and dissociates H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    nearly thermoneutrally (+0.077 eV). Therefore ·OH is held on Ru rather than on the Fe. This work establishes radical buffering by independent single‐atom populations in confined micropores as a design principle for controlling selectivity in radical‐mediated catalysis.

title: An Acyclic Two‐Coordinate Stannyliumylidene Enables SnII/SnIV Redox Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Main‐group redox catalysis hinges on a fundamental trade‐off, that is, reactive p‐block centres must be stable enough to isolate, yet flexible enough to cycle through oxidation states. In this regard, two‐coordinate stannyliumylidene ions with an accessible lone pair and vacant p‐orbital offer an attractive ambiphilic platform for engaging in redox processes. To date, most reported examples remain confined to π‐ or heteroatom‐donor‐stabilized rigid frameworks, and the isolation of a genuinely two‐coordinate acyclic stannyliumylidene has remained elusive. Herein, we report the synthesis and isolation of a two‐coordinate, acyclic, mono‐N‐heterocyclic‐carbene‐stabilized stannyliumylidene paired with a weakly coordinating [B(3,5‐(CF
                    3
                    )
                    2
                    C
                    6
                    H
                    3
                    )
                    4
                    ]
                    −
                    anion. Stripped of additional donor stabilization, the tin centre is rendered highly electrophilic while maintaining an accessible lone pair. This enhanced electrophilicity enabled capture of a stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct, the first structurally characterized ketone‐bound tetryliumylidene intermediate that is directly implicated in a catalytic cycle. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, combining experimental results with theoretical calculations, reveal an Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox manifold that drives catalytic turnover. Together, these results significantly expand the landscape of tin‐based redox catalysis and highlight that accessing stable low‐valent stannyliumylidene ions with a minimal coordination number and weaker donor stabilization is a feasible approach for unlocking transition‐metal‐like redox behaviour at the tin centre.

title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aldoximes are vital feedstocks in the fields of medicine, agriculture, and industry, yet their conventional synthesis suffers from high environmental costs and carbon footprints. Here, we report a direct electrocatalytic route to acetaldoxime via CO and NO
                    3
                    −
                    co‐reduction. The C–N coupling efficiency in this process hinges on the kinetic match between CO reduction and NO
                    3
                    −
                    reduction. Acetaldoxime synthesis exemplifies this challenge: sluggish C–C dimerization contrasts with rapid NO
                    3
                    −
                    RR, leading to over‐reduction of nitrogen species to NH
                    3
                    . We hypothesized that a confinement strategy could selectively promote C–C dimerization and enrich acetaldehyde intermediate, thereby facilitating oximation. Ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles were encapsulated within SBA‐15 mesopores to selectively accelerate the dimerization step. Combined operando Raman and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal that the confined Cu lowers the overpotential for the key C
                    2
                    intermediate to align with that for NH
                    2
                    OH generation, enabling efficient C–N coupling to acetaldoxime. The optimized Cu@SBA‐15 catalyst achieves an acetaldoxime production rate of 255.1 mmol g
                    cat.
                    −
                    1
                    h
                    −
                    1
                    (partial current density: 24.6 mA cm
                    −
                    2
                    ). This work establishes a sustainable pathway toward aldoximes, aligning with green chemistry principles while expanding the toolbox for electrocatalytic C–N bond formation.

title: Guide DNAs Program Enzyme for Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA Without Target Denaturation and Amplification
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is fragmented, tumor‐derived cell‐free double‐stranded DNA (dsDNA) whose low abundance and limited sequence accessibility complicate detection under mild conditions. Here we show that guide DNAs (gDNAs) can program an exonuclease to interrogate native dsDNA under mild conditions and convert this access into a single‐molecule fluorescence readout. We found that gDNA 5′‐terminal chemistry regulates λ exonuclease (λExo) recruitment. Among those termini, anionic 5′‐phosphate and 5′‐carboxyl‐C10 phosphate enabled the strongest target‐dependent processing. Molecular simulations suggested a possible structural basis for these activity differences based on terminal positioning within the catalytic pocket. Coupling the optimized 5′‐carboxyl‐C10 phosphate gDNA with 10–23 DNAzyme turnover generated a single‐molecule fluorescence readout without target nucleic‐acid amplification. The assay detected dsDNA down to 10 fM across 10–1000 fM, showed a statistically significant response at an epidermal growth factor receptor (
                    EGFR
                    ) L858R mutant fraction of 0.05% under the tested conditions, and was applied to 24 plasma samples (12 from patients with non‐small‐cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 12 from healthy donors), achieving 91.7% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 95.8% accuracy, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.97. This work establishes gDNA‐programmed enzyme access as a route for detecting low‐abundance duplex tumor DNA.

title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO
                    2
                    and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO
                    2
                    hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady‐state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO
                    2
                    hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO
                    2
                    hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO
                    2
                    hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO
                    2
                    activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo‐ and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

title: Thiophenol‐Catalyzed Anti‐Markovnikov Coupling of α‐Methylene‐γ‐Butenolides Under Visible Light: Total Synthesis of Aucklappalide A
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    General methods for the selective
                    anti
                    ‐Markovnikov intermolecular coupling of electron‐poor alkenes remain scarce. Herein, we report a visible‐light‐mediated, photocatalyst‐free strategy for the
                    anti
                    ‐Markovnikov coupling of
                    α
                    ‐methylene‐
                    γ
                    ‐butenolides using a simple formate/thiophenol reaction platform. The method enables the direct synthesis of structurally diverse homo‐ and cross‐coupled disesquiterpenoid architectures from complex sesquiterpenoid lactones, including the first total synthesis of aucklappalide A. Mechanistic investigations support a distinct sulfur‐mediated photochemical manifold involving a thiophenol adduct that provides access to the carbon‐centered radical required for intermolecular C–C bond formation. These findings establish a photocatalyst‐free approach to the redox‐neutral
                    anti
                    ‐Markovnikov coupling of
                    α
                    ‐methylene‐
                    γ
                    ‐butenolides, uncover a previously unrecognized sulfur‐mediated radical manifold enabled by formate/thiophenol photochemistry, and suggest that related sulfur‐centered radical processes may contribute to the biosynthesis of dimeric sesquiterpenoid lactones.

title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis
source: Nature
abstract: Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex
source: Nature
abstract: Poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1–3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
source: Nature
abstract: Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

title: Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract: Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management.

title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li6PS5Cl interface increases the discharge current at which voiding commences tenfold, from 0.2 to 2 mA cm−2 at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm−2 at 30 °C and 8 mA cm−2 at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

title: Photothermal-driven CO2 hydrogenation to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS2–TiO2 catalyst
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Light-driven CO2 hydrogenation to methanol is constrained by insufficient broadband light utilization and inefficient CO2 activation. Herein, we achieve highly efficient photothermal hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS2–TiO2 catalyst, in which MoS2 is anchored on TiO2 to form an intimate interface, and Au nanoparticles (NPs) are deposited on MoS2–TiO2. We demonstrate that the MoS2–TiO2 interface induces the formation of few-layered MoS2 and transfers electrons from TiO2 to MoS2. MoS2 serves as the primary active phase for CO2 hydrogenation, while Au NPs enhance photo-to-heat conversion via the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect, thereby collectively facilitating CO2 activation under mild reaction conditions. Under photothermal conditions at 120°C in a continuous-flow reactor, the catalyst achieves 13.4% CO2 conversion with 84.7% methanol selectivity, and maintains stable performance over 400 hours without observable deactivation, underscoring it among the most competitive photothermal catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.

title: Room temperature giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect in TbMn6Sn6
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The anomalous Hall effect is the transverse voltage response in the presence of out-of-plane magnetization or non-zero Berry curvature, which, traditionally, is modulated by an out-of-plane magnetic field. Here we demonstrate a giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by coplanar magnetic fields in the quantum magnet TbMn6Sn6 at room temperature. The very large Hall conductivity arises in response to an applied in-plane magnetic field and results from the tilting of the ferrimagnetic axis of the Mn and Tb moments to the out of plane direction. With the in-plane magnetic field aligning the ferrimagnetic axis, the Berry curvature induced giant anomalous Hall effect is observed. Further, we show that the in-plane field induced AHE is more pronounced below the temperature induced spin reorientation, showing a 2π periodicity in angular dependent measurements. Unlike the in-plane Hall effect previously observed primarily at low temperatures, the AHE we observe here represents the largest room-temperature response reported in a single material. Our results reveal strong coupling between an in-plane magnetic field and out-of-plane Berry curvature, enabling new opportunities to engineer spintronic and quantum device responses at practical operating temperatures.

title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Electrocyclizations are a fundamental class of pericyclic transformations that can proceed through thermal or photochemical pathways. Although thermal electrocyclizations have been implicated in numerous biosynthetic pathways, there are few examples of enzyme-mediated processes, and the structural requirements for efficient catalysis are poorly understood. Here we develop an artificial photoenzyme for 6π-electrocyclizations (PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3) by introducing ten mutations into a recently reported [2 + 2]-cyclase. PEC1.3 processes diverse acrylanilide substrates with exceptional yields, regiocontrol and stereocontrol. A 1.3-Å crystal structure shows the substrate ideally positioned for energy transfer from a genetically programmed benzophenone triplet sensitizer. Interestingly, hydrogen-bonding interactions that were critical to [2 + 2] cyclase activity were abandoned during evolution of PEC1.3. Instead, the enzyme employs a network of hydrophobic interactions to constrain the substrate into a reactive geometry for selective antarafacial electrocyclization, allowing PEC1.3 to retain activity at cryogenic temperatures where appreciable molecular motions are frozen out. This example of controlled reaction outcomes without polar substrate–enzyme contacts points towards selective conversions of substrates lacking functional handles.

title: Nanocatalytic modulation of thrombin-ferroptosis axis for efficient intervention of ischemic stroke
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Ischemic stroke represents a leading cause of global mortality. Current therapeutic strategies, including recombinant tissue plasminogen activator and mechanical thrombectomy, are constrained by suboptimal recanalization, high recurrence rates, and reperfusion injury. In this work, we initially identified elevated intrathrombotic thrombin as a critical mediator of fibrinolytic resistance and a driver of ferroptosis-related neuronal injury following stroke. To specifically target this thrombin dysregulation, we designed ultrasmall tungsten-based polyoxometalate (W-POM) nanodots capable of penetrating the blood-brain barrier. In addition to their specific reactive oxygen species-scavenging capability, W-POM nanodots primarily modulate thrombin activity and attenuate its pathological signaling. In both thrombin-induced and ischemia-reperfusion injury models, W-POM nanodots significantly improve neurological outcomes by directly suppressing thrombin activity and inhibiting thrombin-driven ferroptosis. Furthermore, W-POM nanodots remodel the thrombotic microenvironment and reduce neuroinflammation, thereby conferring robust neuroprotection. This study highlights the thrombin-ferroptosis pathway as a key mechanistic axis in stroke and introduces a nanotherapeutic platform for targeted thrombin modulation in ischemic stroke therapy.

title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. We implement this principle through an axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion direct laser writing strategy that keeps the depletion zone aligned with the Gaussian excitation focus. Axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion produces isolated lines 56.2 nm wide and resolves gratings with a 150-nm period and a 110-nm linewidth at a 160 μm depth with a numerical aperture of 1.27, while maintaining a 167.3-nm linewidth at 1,400 μm, using a numerical aperture of 1.1. We use axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion to fabricate axially extended mesoscopic optical systems, including 4f systems, vortex phase plates, miniaturized objectives and microlens arrays.

title: Molecular regulation and recurrent evolution of fungal bet-hedging conidiation
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Bet-hedging (BH) mitigates risk in fluctuating environments by promoting phenotypic diversity within a single genotype. Fungi exhibit remarkable phenotypic plasticity, such as conidiation polymorphism. Here, we show that entomopathogenic Metarhizium species produce either monomorphic or dimorphic conidia, which exhibit marked size variation to support different BH strategies. The large cylindrical and small ovoid conidia produced by the same species possess complementary advantages that facilitate adaptation to different conditions. Large conidia are heavily pigmented, ultraviolet-resistant, and highly virulent, whereas small conidia, produced either on separate phialides or atop large ones, germinate faster and resist bacteria better. These complementary traits represent a classic, yet previously unsuspected, diversified BH strategy. Mechanistic analysis revealed distinct gene expression patterns between morphotypes, leading to the identification of a transcription factor and a lipid-droplet surface protein that play key roles in governing dimorphic conidiation and pigmentation. Phylogenomic reconstruction revealed that later-diverging species reverted to an ancestral, monomorphic medium-spore state, indicating a recurrence of the conservative BH strategy. Pairwise experimental evolution confirmed that monomorphic populations have a fitness advantage under fluctuating ultraviolet irradiation. Our findings establish the BH mechanism in conidiation and reveal evolutionary experimentation with reversion across fungal speciation.

title: Nucleophile–electrophile chemistry produces a stable interphase for long-Life anode-Less lithium metal batteries
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Anode-less lithium (Li) metal batteries (ALLMBs) represent the optimal cell architecture for maximizing energy density, yet their practical viability is severely hindered by poor cycling life. This limitation stems from the unstable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI), which drives continuous parasitic reactions with Li metal and induces severe interfacial degradation. Here we report a nucleophile–electrophile bridging strategy to construct a robust, passivating SEI that enables long-term stable cycling of ALLMBs. By leveraging a nucleophilic substitution mechanism, electron-rich organic species derived from the solvent, acting as nucleophiles, are covalently bridged by electron-deficient, boron-centred electrophiles derived from the anion. This molecular-level integration overcomes the inherent fragility of the SEI organic phase, generating mechanically robust oligoborates that resist interfacial degradation, along with lithium fluoride (LiF) nanocrystals nucleated in-situ to facilitate rapid Li+ transport. The resulting oligoborate–LiF hybrid SEI enables highly reversible Li plating/stripping and remarkably extends the ALLMB cycling life by 12-fold, maintaining 80% capacity over 300 cycles. The superior cyclability is maintained even under stringent practical conditions (high cathode loading, lean electrolyte supply, and pouch-cell operation). This work establishes a fundamentally new paradigm in interphase engineering, paving the way for high-energy, reliable ALLMBs.

title: Polyanion‐Modulated Vanadium‐Doped Ammonium Iron Phosphate Framework from Spent LiFePO4 for Lattice Oxygen‐Participated Water Oxidation
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Promoting the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) offers an effective route to improving the efficiency of water electrolysis. However, achieving efficient LOM operation in structurally stable catalysts remains challenging. To address this challenge, we report a microwave‐assisted upcycling strategy using spent LiFePO
                    4
                    as a lithium‐deficient precursor. The cycling‐induced lithium deficiency facilitates structural reorganization into a polyanion‐modulated vanadium‐doped ammonium iron phosphate hydroxide hydrate (S‐VAFP) without residual Li‐containing impurities. The resulting S‐VAFP features a three‐dimensional polyanionic framework composed of FeO
                    6
                    octahedra vertex‐linked with PO
                    4
                    tetrahedra, forming one‐dimensional channels that promote electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This architecture tunes Fe─O covalency, weakens Fe─(O─P) linkages, and drives in situ reconstruction into a catalytically active amorphous phase, thereby facilitating lattice oxygen participation. Chemical probe experiments and
                    18
                    O isotope‐labeling DEMS further verify the AEM–LOM coupled OER pathway. Benefiting from this structure‐guided LOM activation, S‐VAFP delivers an overpotential of 250 mV at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    with a Tafel slope of 47.2 mV dec
                    ‒1
                    . An assembled anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) cell achieves 1.72 V at 1 A cm
                    −2
                    with stability exceeding 1000 h. Overall, this work establishes polyanion‐mediated electronic modulation as an effective strategy for designing stable iron phosphate electrocatalysts with enhanced lattice oxygen participation.

title: Directed Perovskite‐to‐Fullerene Electron Shuttle for 27.2% Inverted Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Although C
                    60
                    is almost exclusively used in the electron transport layers of high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), its weak affinity and unfavorable energy level alignment with perovskite lead to weak contact and mismatch in the conduction band level at the perovskite/C
                    60
                    interface, thereby limiting further improvement of device efficiency as well as compromising device long‐term operational stability. We synthesized an
                    n
                    ‐type Pyridinium molecule, 2,7‐di(pyridin‐4‐yl)benzo[lmn][3,8]phenanthroline‐1,3,6,8(2H,7H)‐tetraone dihydroiodide (PPTHI), and used it as the interfacial electron‐selective contact in inverted PSCs. The pyridinium iodide head unit in the PPTHI anchored to the halide vacancies and coordinated with the exposed lead. Moreover, the π‐conjugated core renders desirable electron‐transport capability, and the
                    n
                    ‐type interfacial modulator can also serve as an electron shuttle between perovskite and the C
                    60
                    electron transport layer. The improved electron extraction, optimized energetic, and passivated top surface translated to reduced V
                    OC
                    losses, leading to a certified stabilized power output efficiency of 26.54% and a champion device with an efficiency of 27.2% and a fill factor of 87.17%. Moreover, inverted PSCs incorporating the electron shuttle maintained over 80% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking.

title: Operando Pressure Monitoring, EIS, and X‐Ray Imaging of Solid‐State Sodium‐Sulfur Batteries — Insights into Chemo‐Mechanical Degradation Mechanisms
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In this study, we introduce a multi‐modal
                    operando
                    platform that combines cell stack pressure monitoring, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and x‐ray imaging to unravel the chemo‐mechanical aging processes in sulfide‐based solid‐state sodium‐sulfur (ssNa||S) cells. Despite their promising theoretical capacity and resource abundance, the mechanisms that limit the full performance of ssNa||S batteries are still poorly understood. To address this issue, we employ a new multi‐modal
                    operando
                    setup optimized for solid‐state cells. By comparing cells with different electrolytes, Na
                    3
                    PS
                    4
                    (NPS), a multiphase electrolyte Na
                    2
                    S‐P
                    2
                    S
                    5
                    ‐NaCl (NPS‐Cl), and Na
                    3
                    SbS
                    4
                    (NSbS),
                    operando
                    over the course of 50 cycles, we monitor slowly evolving aging effects that are found to be correlated with the electrolyte composition. For NPS, the combination of low interfacial stability against sodium and reduced ionic conductivity causes the electrochemical activity to be concentrated in localized regions, leading to sodium plating‐like behavior as the dominant degradation mechanism. In contrast, the chloride‐containing NPS‐Cl enhances the interfacial stability and mitigates dendrite formation. These findings provide valuable insights for the materials development of sulfide‐based electrolytes for ssNa||S cells and demonstrate the capability of combined operando diagnostics to resolve complex chemo‐mechanical phenomena that influence solid‐state battery performance.

title: Synergistic Interfacial and Subsurface Stabilization of O3‐Type Na‐Ni‐Fe‐Mn‐O Cathodes through Integrated Zr Modification
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Surface degradation, electrolyte‐derived hydrogen fluoride (HF) attack, and anisotropic phase evolution limit the stability of O3‐type sodium cathodes. An integrated Zr‐based surface/subsurface strategy is developed for Na[Ni
                    0.3

X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, Mössbauer spectroscopy, and hybrid‐functional calculations indicate Ni/Fe‐dominated cationic redox, nearly tetravalent Mn, and no major lattice‐oxygen redox contribution. Coulomb–Buckingham calculations suggest that Zr incorporation at Mn sites is energetically favored near the surface within the adopted model. The Na

title: Direct Solar Storage and On‐Demand Power via Threshold‐Matched Silicon Photovoltaics and Dual‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Direct integration of photovoltaics with batteries is attractive for energy‐autonomous mobile platforms, but mismatched photovoltaic output and battery charging requirements, limited high‐rate capability, and low‐temperature degradation can necessitate intermediate power electronics and restrict burst‐power delivery. Here, a threshold‐matched silicon photovoltaic–dual‐ion battery (PV–DIB) architecture is demonstrated by directly coupling a voltage‐ and current‐tailored crystalline‐silicon photovoltaic module with a high‐voltage dual‐ion battery pouch cell. Under one‐sun illumination, the photovoltaic module supplies ≈72 mA at the battery charging threshold, enabling direct charging without intermediate power‐conversion hardware. This matching establishes two complementary operating regimes: solar‐sustained operation when photovoltaic current meets the load demand and on‐demand battery assistance when the load exceeds the photovoltaic input. The integrated system delivers a maximum power density of 11,430 W kg
                    −1
                    at 40.83 mA cm
                    −2
                    , maintains stable operation under drone‐relevant dynamic load profiles, and the DIB retains 5,088 W kg
                    −1
                    at −10°C. Indoor and outdoor flight demonstrations validate direct solar energy storage and burst‐power delivery, establishing threshold matching as a practical design strategy for power‐electronics‐minimized, energy‐autonomous mobile systems.

title: Broadband Aeolian Vibration Harvesting and Electrical‐Damping‐Induced Suppression via Triboelectric‐Electromagnetic Coupling Mechanism
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Overhead transmission lines have long faced dual threats: a scarcity of power for sensor nodes and fatigue caused by aeolian vibrations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a synergistic strategy that integrates energy harvesting with vibration suppression, transforming vibration energy dissipation into a coupled process of electrical energy conversion and vibration suppression. Based on this strategy, a triboelectric‐electromagnetic coupling device (TECD) is developed. By leveraging the complementary frequency‐domain characteristics of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) and electromagnetic generators (EMGs), as well as the electrical damping generated during the energy conversion process, the device achieves deep synergy between wideband energy harvesting and vibration suppression. Experimental results demonstrate that the TECD can stably charge a 47 µF capacitor to a 5.2 V supply threshold at any frequency within the 5–50 Hz range, reaching a peak output power of up to 287.28 mW. Simultaneously, the associated electrical damping effectively suppresses vibrations, reducing the vibration acceleration of the primary structure by 86% under 30 Hz excitation. Built upon this device, an integrated harvesting‐suppression‐sensing system is constructed, paving a new path for self‐powered state monitoring and structural protection of transmission lines.

title: Interface‐to‐Bulk Grain Regulation Enables Sb2(S,Se)3 Solar Cells Exceeding 11% Efficiency
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Antimony selenosulfide (Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    ) represents an emerging thin‐film photovoltaic absorber owing to the excellent stability, tunable bandgap (1.1–1.7 eV), and high light absorption coefficient (> 10
                    5
                    cm
                    −1
                    ). Hydrothermally deposited Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    solar cells have broken the 10% efficiency bottleneck, yet as‐prepared Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    films suffer from small grains (typically ∼400 nm) with abundant grain boundaries (GBs) that introduce dense defect states, inducing severe non‐radiative recombination and hindering further efficiency enhancement. Here we develop an interface‐to‐bulk grain regulation strategy to achieve ultra‐large (exceeding 3 µm) columnar grains spanning the entire absorber. This strategy combines buried‐interface Sb pre‐deposition to tailor initial hydrothermal deposition and rear‐interface Se‐mediated two‐step post‐annealing to drive grain coalescence and growth through a sequential infiltration‐reaction‐coalescence mechanism. We also found that this grain engineering also leads to the passivation of bulk deep‐level and interfacial defects, and optimized heterojunction band alignment, which collectively suppresses non‐radiative recombination and in turn delivers an ultralow open‐circuit voltage deficit of 0.483 V. Consequently, the ultra‐large‐grain Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    solar cell delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 11.04%, which is the highest efficiency ever reported for antimony chalcogenide‐based solar cells. This study establishes an integrated strategy for regulating grain growth in Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    films toward efficient devices.

title: A Spin‐Crossover Neutral‐Site Perovskite Ferroelectric
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Perovskites have emerged as a globally researched family of multifunctional materials, benefiting from their rich physical properties. However, despite extensive investigations into their ferroelectric and magnetic properties, the coexistence of ferroelectricity and spin crossover (SCO) within perovskites remains largely unexplored. Herein, by combining perovskites and coordination polymers (CPs), we designed the first perovskite SCO ferroelectric, [Fe(4‐ATA)
                    3

                    6

                    3

                    6

                    6
