title: Topology‐Encoded Polymer Networks for Thermo‐Responsive Wrinkling With Dynamic Diffraction Tunability
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Thermo‐responsive wrinkles provide a scalable route to adaptive optical surfaces. However, achieving thermally tunable structural color with high diffraction efficiency remains challenging, limiting their applications in optical devices and information encryption. This challenge arises from conventional wrinkle systems relying on empirical macroscopic parameters and lacking molecular‐level design principles based on network topology. Herein, we propose a crosslinker chain‐length programming strategy to construct thermally responsive optical wrinkled surfaces with encoded polymer network topology. By tuning bismaleimide crosslinker chain length, network topology and thermomechanical response are regulated, directing thermally induced surface instability into oriented periodic wrinkles with programmable structural color and diffraction efficiency. Using crosslinker chain length and prestrain as design variables, a two‐dimensional diffraction efficiency design map is constructed to delineate diffractive and non‐diffractive regimes, achieving a maximum diffraction efficiency of 22.7%. Chain length‐dependent UV‐induced maleimide dimerization enables spatially resolved orthogonal patterning, allowing hidden information to be written and read out optically under manual stretching without external devices. Dynamic Diels–Alder (D–A) reversibility supports partial wrinkle amplitude erasure, enabling post‐read information invalidation. This study bridges molecularly encoded polymer network topology and macroscopic optical performance, providing molecular‐level design principles for multistimuli‐responsive optical platforms and advanced anti‐counterfeiting materials.

title: Nonclassical Electrostriction: The Insights From X‐Ray Absorption Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Nonclassical electrostriction (NCES) has emerged in a growing class of ionic solids that exhibit electromechanical responses far exceeding predictions of the conventional Newnham scaling law despite moderate dielectric permittivity and high elastic modulus. Unlike classical electrostriction, which is associated with nearly uniform anharmonic deformation of the crystal lattice, NCES originates from the field‐induced reorganization of a small population of locally distorted structural units. This Review examines the unique role of x‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy in identifying the electromechanically active structural units, resulting in the understanding of atomistic mechanisms underlying this behavior. Element‐specific x‐ray absorption near edge structure and extended XAFS (EXAFS) measurements identify local symmetry breaking, defect‐associated elastic dipoles, multimodal bond‐length distributions, and strongly anharmonic bonds that remain “hidden” from average‐structure probes. Field‐modulated, high energy resolution, and differential XAFS further isolate the minority structural units directly responsible for macroscopic strain. Aliovalent and isovalent dopants are shown to produce distinct microscopic mechanisms, involving vacancy‐associated static and dynamic elastic dipoles, respectively, embedding strong attributes of anharmonicity. These results establish local structure and bond dynamics as key descriptors of NCES and highlight in situ, stimulus‐modulated XAFS as a powerful route for uncovering and ultimately controlling electromechanical coupling in defect‐engineered materials.

title: Learning to Program Dimple‐Encoded Strips for Morphing Architectures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Programmable morphing structures that translate local mechanical states into global shape transformations enable deployable, adaptive, and reconfigurable systems. Dimple‐encoded elastic strips provide a minimal platform in which arrays of bistable dimples can collectively program large bending deformation. Yet the nonlinear mapping from the encoded geometry to the final configuration makes inverse design challenging. Here, we report a learning‐enabled strategy for programming dimple‐encoded strips with prescribed morphing profiles and using them as building blocks for higher‐level morphing architectures. Finite‐element simulations are converted into centerline‐based tangent‐field representations to train a one‐dimensional convolutional neural‐network surrogate that maps local dimple encoding and strip geometry to global shape. The trained surrogate enables gradient‐based inverse design of target morphologies, with optimized designs validated by independent simulations and physical prototypes. Variable‐width strip modules expand the accessible shape space and enable width‐conditioned curvature programming. Rotational tessellation of programmed strip modules creates dome‐like morphing shells, while hierarchical integration of curvature‐programmed strips with folding modules yields an artifical flower exhibiting sequential opening through dimple switching. These results establish dimple‐encoded strips as learnable building blocks that connect local bistable encoding, inverse design, and hierarchical shape formation, providing a route toward task‐specific morphing components for soft robotics, adaptive interfaces, and deployable structures.

title: Self‐Assembled Nanoplatform for Modulating the ATP‐Adenosine Pathway and CD8+ T Cell Metabolism to Potentiate Radiotherapy‐Mediated Antitumor Immunity
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Radiotherapy (RT) is one of the primary clinical modalities for tumor treatment, yet its therapeutic efficacy is restricted by post‐RT immunosuppression and impaired function of tumor‐infiltrating cytotoxic T lymphocytes. Herein, we fabricate self‐assembled nanoparticles based on sodium metatungstate (POM1) and spermidine (Spd), followed by polyethylene glycol (PEG) modification to enhance biocompatibility (denoted as POM1‐Spd/PEG). Structural characterization and molecular simulations confirm that the core POM1‐Spd complex is assembled via electrostatic and van der Waals interactions, with each POM1 cluster stably anchoring two Spd molecules to form a dimeric supramolecular architecture. Benefiting from these weak intermolecular interactions, POM1‐Spd/PEG can efficiently disassemble in the weakly acidic tumor microenvironment to release free POM1 and Spd. Notably, we uncover that POM1 possesses unrecognized dual functional properties, which act as both a potent radiosensitizer to amplify RT‐induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) and an efficient CD39 inhibitor that prevents the conversion of ICD‐released ATP to immunosuppressive adenosine (ADO), thereby reversing ADO‐mediated tumor immunosuppression and sustaining robust antitumor immune activation. Furthermore, the released Spd upregulates fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial ATP synthesis in CD8
                    +
                    T cells, consequently boosting their proliferation and cytotoxic effector functions. When combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors, this strategy can effectively trigger systemic antitumor immunity to further enhance therapeutic efficacy and suppress the growth and metastasis of distant tumors. Collectively, our work develops a distinctive self‐assembled nanoplatform capable of achieving radiosensitization, regulating the ATP‐ADO pathway, and improving CD8
                    +
                    T cell metabolism, offering a promising approach to amplify RT efficacy by remodeling antitumor immunity.

title: Bioinspired Membrane Fusion–Gated Hydrogel Biosensor for Extraction‐Free Viral RNA Detection of Infectious Influenza Virus
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Emerging infectious diseases driven by zoonotic spillover demand rapid and reliable molecular diagnostics for pathogen identification and surveillance. However, conventional nucleic acid diagnostics cannot distinguish infectious virions from nonviable RNA fragments, limiting infectivity‐resolved virus identification. Here, we report a bioinspired membrane‐coated hydrogel (Memgel) sensor that enables extraction‐free molecular detection of influenza virus while distinguishing fusion‐competent virions from noninfectious viral material. The platform integrates a cell‐mimetic supported lipid bilayer with a polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel matrix encapsulating recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) reagents. Under endosome‐mimicking acidic conditions, hemagglutinin‐mediated membrane fusion selectively delivers viral genomic RNA from infectious virions into the hydrogel matrix, triggering sequence‐specific amplification while suppressing signals from free viral RNA fragments. As a proof of concept, the Memgel sensor was evaluated for the detection of influenza A (H9N2) in simulated nasal fluid and raw milk matrices, achieving a limit of detection of 10
                    1.23
                    TCID
                    50
                    mL
                    −
                    1
                    while maintaining robust detection performance without RNA extraction. Coupled with a portable fluorescence reader, the system demonstrates compatibility with compact fluorescence‐based readout for future point‐of‐care implementation. This fusion‐gated sensing strategy provides a materials‐based framework for infectivity‐resolved molecular diagnostics of emerging viral pathogens.

title: Metal‐Chelating Molecule‐Enabled Multidentate Molecular Bridge Engineering of the Buried Interface for High‐Performance Fully Printed Carbon‐Based Perovskite Solar Modules
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Carbon‐based perovskite solar modules (C‐PSMs) provide a scalable and metal‐electrode‐free platform for stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet their efficiencies remain constrained by defective and mechanically fragile buried SnO
                    2
                    /perovskite interfaces. Conventional interfacial modifiers generally rely on limited coordination, making it difficult to simultaneously achieve robust passivation and strong interfacial adhesion. Here, we introduce two metal‐chelating molecules to construct multidentate molecular bridges at the buried interface in C‐PSMs. Diglycine disodium (DDS), although capable of coordinating with both SnO
                    2
                    and perovskite, exhibits weak configurational selectivity because multiple interfacial coordination modes are energetically accessible, preventing stable bilateral bridge formation. In contrast, tetrasodium iminodisuccinate (IDS) coordinates with both SnO
                    2
                    and perovskite, constructing a robust bilateral molecular bridge, suppressing interfacial defects, enhancing charge transfer, and interfacial adhesion. Consequently, the fully printed 30 × 30 cm
                    2
                    IDS C‐PSMs achieve a record efficiency of 19.26% with an active area of 563.78 cm
                    2
                    (certified 18.04%, with a mask‐defined area of 487.6 cm
                    2
                    ), which represents the highest reported PCE for a device of this size and architecture. The unencapsulated IDS C‐PSM retains over 90% of its initial efficiency after 1130 h of maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C and over 85% after 2184 h under damp‐heat conditions (85°C and 85% RH).

title: Enhanced Molecular‐Structure Dual‐Recognition by Enzyme‐Embedded Metal‐Phenolic Networks for Wearable Plant Sensing of Pesticides
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    On‐site monitoring of plant health using enzyme‐based wearable sensors is essential for sustainable agriculture, yet inherent enzyme instability and poor molecular recognition remain major obstacles. Here, we present a robust plant‐wearable hydrogel sensor based on an acetylcholinesterase‐embedded metal‐phenolic network (AChE@MPN) to overcome these limitations through a dual‐recognition strategy, markedly improving stability and selectivity relative to conventional sensors. The MPN protects the enzyme's native conformation, maintaining catalytic kinetics comparable to those of the free enzyme. Within this architecture, the dual‐recognition strategy integrates metal‐assisted adsorption with enzymatic recognition, engaging pesticide molecules through synergistic P‐O‐Zr coordination, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking to yield a 1.41‐fold higher response to phoxim than that obtained with free AChE. Notably, the AChE@MPN exhibits an approximately 88‐fold higher binding affinity for phoxim than for its nonaromatic analog malathion, indicating that the signal gain originates from selective enrichment. These features enable the sensor to discriminate phoxim from interfering substances, with a limit of detection of 2 ng mL
                    −1
                    , and to perform on‐site monitoring of phoxim degradation on living tomato plants. This dual‐recognition design offers a general strategy for pesticide monitoring and may inspire plant‐sensing innovations for sustainable agriculture.

title: Quenching or Accelerating Large‐Scale Surface Reconstruction by the Lightest Element: Facet‐Dependent Hydrogen‐Induced Reconstruction (HIR)
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Adsorbate‐induced surface reconstruction is believed to be a critical determinant of catalyst performance under operando conditions. The Pd–Ag bimetallic catalyst, used industrially for selective acetylene hydrogenation, is thought to undergo hydrogen‐induced surface reconstruction (HIR) that exposes Pd active sites. However, the kinetic origin of HIR remains unknown because hydrogen is difficult to image. Here, using large‐scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we resolve the kinetics of H‐driven reconstruction. On Pd‐covered Ag surfaces, reconstruction initially involves Pd–Ag exchange at domain peripheries and Ag atoms popping up to encapsulate exposed Pd. This process is faster on (100) than on (111). Hydrogen suppresses reconstruction on (111) above 0.3 ML, but accelerates Pd dispersion and encapsulation on (100) mediated by transient Pd–H pair formation. This facet dependence arises from hydrogen‐induced kinetic hindrance of edge Pd diffusion away from Pd domains on (111). Analysis of MD‐derived surface structures further shows that the Pd3 triangular surface pattern favors selective acetylene hydrogenation, confirming HIR's role in determining active‐site structure. These findings provide the first evidence for facet‐dependent, large‐scale surface reconstruction induced by the lightest element and establish HIR as a key determinant of catalytic activity and selectivity.

title: Copper‐Catalyzed Enantioconvergent 1,4‐Difunctionalization of Homoallylic and Homopropargylic Alcohols via Radical‐Relay Deoxygenation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Despite the long‐recognized structural diversity and accessibility of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols as synthetic building blocks, their deoxygenative radical difunctionalization remains a formidable challenge due to the lack of a linkage strategy integrating the respective functionalization of non‐adjacent hydroxyl and alkene/alkyne groups. Herein, we present an efficient platform for the deoxygenative radical 1,4‐difunctionalization of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols through an unprecedented remote hydrogen atom transfer‐triggered radical‐relay deoxygenation process. Utilizing 1,3‐benzodithiolylium as an effective hydroxyl‐activating reagent, copper‐catalyzed enantioconvergent 1,4‐perfluoroalkylamidation and 1,4‐cyanoperfluoroalkylation have been achieved with excellent regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

title: Fast‐Discharge‐Induced Non‐Equilibrium Phase Transition in Ni‐Rich Layered Oxide Cathode at High Voltage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The rapid adoption of electric vehicles necessitates lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) that can sustain extreme fast charging (XFC) without rapid degradation. Ni‐rich layered cathodes deliver high energy density, yet their poor stability under high‐rate operation limits practical deployment and the mechanistic origin of fast capacity decay remains poorly understood. Here, using high time‐resolved
                    operando
                    XRD, together with theoretical analyses, we reveal that a rate‐dependent non‐equilibrium H3→H2 phase transition under rapid discharge (≥4 C) induces huge lattice displacement and nanoscale strain, which significantly lower the migration barrier for Ni, thereby promoting irreversible rock‐salt phase formation and structural collapse. Importantly, guided by this mechanistic understanding, we propose a cycling protocol introducing a brief low‐rate discharge step at high voltage (4.5 V→4.0 V), which effectively suppresses the detrimental H2+H3 phase separation and generation of internal stress. Compared to that of the cell under constant high cycling rates (6 C), the capacity retention improves 29% for the one with optimized discharge procedure after 1000 cycles. These results clarify the underneath electrochemical–mechanical degradation behavior of Ni‐rich layered cathodes at different rates (1/3 C, 1 C, 4 C, and 6 C), providing practical guidance for designing durable batteries with superior fast‐charging abilities.

title: Heteroatom‐Modulated Aggregation of Diketopyrrolopyrrole Derivatives by Single‐Atom Substitution to Construct NIR‐II‐Absorbing Photothermal Agents With Over 90% Efficiency
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic small‐molecule photothermal materials with second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) absorption have attracted enormous interest for biomedical applications, yet simultaneously achieving strong NIR‐II absorption and high photothermal conversion efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report to conduct the heteroatom‐modulated aggregation of diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) derivatives (named as DAQ‐T and DAQ‐Fu) by single‐atom substitution to construct high‐performance NIR‐II‐absorbing photothermal agents. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen‐for‐sulfur substitution precisely modulates electrostatic potential distributions and tailors intermolecular π–π interactions by leveraging the distinct electronegativities of chalcogens, driving a transformation from
                    H
                    ‐aggregation in DAQ‐T to
                    J
                    ‐aggregation in DAQ‐Fu. The resulting
                    J
                    ‐aggregated DAQ‐Fu nanoparticles feature a distinct absorption band at 1064 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 3.26 × 10
                    4
                    L mol
                    −1
                    cm
                    −1
                    , and exhibit an outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency of 92.4%. This photothermal effect exerts potent antitumor efficacy by regulating apoptosis and immune‐related signaling pathways, enabling the synergy of photothermal therapy and as‐induced immunogenic cell death to suppress both primary and distant tumors growth with about 90% and 63% inhibition rates, respectively, under biocompatible irradiation. This work demonstrates atom‐precise aggregation modulation, offering a promising pathway to engineer NIR‐II‐absorbing organic small‐molecule photothermal agents for synergistic photothermal cancer immunotherapy.

title: Mechanism of Alkene Skeletal Isomerization in Zeolites Revealed by Coupled‐Cluster Accurate Free‐Energy Simulations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The mechanism of Brønsted acid‐catalyzed transformations in zeolites is generally described in terms of carbocationic intermediates, yet their thermodynamic stability and mechanistic role remain controversial. Resolving this issue requires chemically accurate free‐energy simulations, which are beyond the reach of conventional density functional theory (DFT) and prohibitively expensive at the coupled‐cluster level. Here, we combine a cluster‐based QM/QM ‐learning strategy with a machine‐learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to enable molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with near‐CCSD(T) accuracy. Applied to the skeletal isomerization of
                    n
                    ‐butene in chabazite, the resulting free‐energy surfaces (FESs) reveal a mechanistic picture that differs qualitatively from that predicted by generalized‐gradient approximation (GGA) functionals. Rather than proceeding through persistent carbocationic intermediates, the reaction is governed by a cascade of highly transient ionic configurations, while protonated methylcyclopropane (PMCP) is identified as a short‐lived reactive configuration rather than a genuine metastable intermediate. These findings provide a more physically consistent description of one of the prototypical reactions in zeolite catalysis. More generally, the methodology introduced here provides a practical route toward chemically accurate free‐energy simulations of heterogeneous catalytic reactions involving highly reactive charged species, opening the way to quantitative mechanistic studies of complex catalytic processes.

title: The Self‐Powered Nanofiltration Membrane Driven by Pulsed Pressure for Efficient Selective Separation of Na+/Ca2+
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge‐like pore structure, a narrow pore‐size distribution, and a high
                    β
                    ‐phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca
                    2+
                    rejection and a Na
                    +
                    /Ca
                    2+
                    separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an “electrostatic–piezoelectric synergistic enhancement” separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Solvation‐Directed Electric Double Layer Formation in Low‐Concentration Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The electric double layer (EDL) governs interfacial stability in lithium metal batteries, yet its rational design remains constrained by concentrated electrolytes or complex solvent systems. Here we demonstrate that the EDL in low‐concentration electrolytes (LCEs) can be rationally programmed through anion selection based on their solvation behavior, decoupling interfacial stability from the heavy consumption of lithium salts and sophisticated solvent blends. By systematically screening anions with distinct Li
                    +
                    ‐anion coordination strengths and steric profiles, we formulate a mixed‐anion LCE and uncover a fundamental principle: large, weakly coordinatinganions (WCAs) accumulate at the interface to form a persistent charge‐shielding layer, whereas small, strongly coordinating anions (SCAs) are dynamically driven deeper into the Helmholtz region under polarization, where they actively modulate interfacial (de)solvation kinetics. This solvation‐defined division of labor creates a rationally designed, self‐adaptive EDL that couples electrostatic stabilization with interfacial chemistry. Beyond offering a high‐performance LCE formulation, this work establishes a direct and mechanistic linkage between bulk solvation architecture and interfacial EDL organization in dilute electrolytes, revealing that the EDL can itself be programmed through anion‐specific solvation motifs to dictate interfacial stability, introducing a design paradigm for materially efficient electrolyte engineering based on solvation‐directed EDL formation.

title: Metal–Backboned Architectures Enable Magneto–Spin–Charge Engineering for High–Performance Li–CO2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Simultaneous CO
                    2
                    conversion and high–energy–density energy storage are urgently needed for sustainable energy systems where Li–CO
                    2
                    batteries provide an ideal solution, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish CO
                    2
                    redox kinetics. Emerging metal–backboned molecules, which contain numerous metal atoms as catalytically active sites, are expected to accelerate CO
                    2
                    reduction reaction kinetics due to their unique architectures and properties. Herein, we report a novel mixed–valence cobalt–backboned polymer with effective spin manipulation as an efficient electrocatalyst and conductive scaffold for Li–CO
                    2
                    batteries, which enables a low overpotential of 1.06 V and outstanding stable cycling over 2700 h. An external magnetic field drives Co centers from low–spin to high–spin configuration and enhances intermetallic intervalence charge transfer, synergistically strengthening CO
                    2
                    adsorption and activation by increasing unpaired electron orbital occupancy and facilitating electron transfer to CO
                    2
                    antibonding orbitals. This work establishes metal–backboned architectures as a versatile platform for spin–charge cooperative engineering, opening a new avenue for kinetically accelerated next–generation energy storage systems.

title: Manganese‐Catalyzed Electrochemical Nitrogenative‐Oxygenative Cleavage of Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Herein, we report a manganese‐catalyzed electrochemical nitrogenative‐oxygenative scission of olefins to nitriles and carbonyls. Mechanistic and kinetic studies reveal distinct precatalyst‐activation and productive‐turnover regimes, and support conversion of the manganese precursor into a mixed‐valent oxo‐bridged dimanganese(III/IV) species, followed by azide‐dependent formation of a product‐forming manganese species. Notably, polyunsaturated substrates can undergo alkene‐chemoselective cleavage with preferential reaction at the more substituted C═C bond, while the present protocol enables unprecedented reactivity towards activated and unactivated alkenes with broad functional‐group tolerance.

title: Electric‐Field‐Manipulated Reaction Pathway Engineering in Lupinus micranthus‐Like High‐Entropy Alloy Nanowires for Direct Alcohol Fuel Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic alcohol oxidation in direct fuel cells is constrained by CO poisoning and insufficient hydroxyl generation at low potentials. Here we show that anisotropic PtFeCoIrRhCu high‐entropy alloy nanowires with
                    Lupinus micranthus
                    ‐like morphology generate a local electric field through coupling of strain‐induced lattice distortion with charge redistribution, enabling a directional capture‐migration‐dissociation relay of interfacial water for efficient low‐potential hydroxyl generation, in which H
                    2
                    O is preferentially captured at Fe/Co sites, migrates under field polarization, and dissociates at Rh/Ir sites. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals that the electric field reorganizes interfacial water into a more ordered hydrogen‐bond network, facilitating water activation. Density functional theory calculations, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry and operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy further demonstrate that the generated hydroxyl species accelerate CO oxidative removal and promote the non‐CO oxidation pathway. Consequently, the catalyst achieves a methanol oxidation mass activity of 3.76 A mg
                    Pt
                    −1
                    , 8.36 times that of Pt/C, together with a direct methanol fuel cell peak power density of 163.06 mW cm
                    −2
                    and stable membrane‐electrode operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    . These findings establish strain–charge coupling as a general strategy for engineering interfacial water activation and directing reaction‐pathway selectivity in multimetallic electrocatalysts.

title: Construction of benzochalcogenaboroles via single-atom editing of boracycles
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Benzoxaborole is arguably the most important boron-based pharmacophore. Since Torssell’s 1957 synthesis, hundreds of benzoxaborole derivatives have emerged, including US Food and Drug Administration-approved tavaborole and crisaborole. However, while peripheral modifications are well studied, synthetic challenges leave isoelectronic core modification less explored, despite its potential to enhance potency and reveal unexplored functions. Here we report a challenging ring expansion of benzoboretenes with elemental chalcogens, where benzoboretenes act as a ‘diradical reservoir’. This synthetic protocol provides a versatile and modular platform for accessing three previously inaccessible classes of benzochalcogenaborole skeletons, in which the oxygen atom of the benzoxaborole core is formally replaced with Se, S or SO2. Preliminary biological evaluation reveals that this ‘O-to-S’ modification confers potent ferroptosis-inhibitory activity. Furthermore, its excellent functional group compatibility enables structure–activity optimization, leading to a 20-fold increase in cellular potency. This research not only expands the chemical space of boron-containing pharmacophores via single-atom ring expansion but also exemplifies how skeletal editing can unlock biological activities.

title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a−1 to ~1000 m a−1 before dropping to ~50 m a−1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s−1), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Anthropogenic pressures on biodiversity necessitate efficient and scalable methods to predict global species distributions. Current species distribution models (SDMs) face challenges with large-scale datasets, complex species associations, and data quality. Here, we introduce EcoVAE, an autoencoder-based generative model that integrates bioclimatic variables with georeferenced occurrences. The model is trained separately for plants, butterflies, and mammals to predict global distributions at both genus and species levels. Through unsupervised learning, EcoVAE captures underlying distribution patterns from large-scale species occurrence data. It achieves high precision and speed, outperforming traditional SDMs in spatial block cross-validation. EcoVAE also reveals signatures of species associations that align with known prey-predator relationships. Taken together, these capacities enable the robust evaluation of global sampling efforts and interpolates distributions in data-limited regions, offering new applications for biodiversity exploration and monitoring.

title: Ion pair acceptor electrolyte for high-energy Li-rich batteries
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Anion-derived inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphases (CEIs) offer a promising solution for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, conventional electrolytes struggle to suppress parasitic side reactions at the high-voltage cathode interface. Herein, a principle for ion pair acceptor electrolyte (IPAE) is proposed utilizing phosphazene-based molecules. Leveraging both anion-π and ion-dipole interactions, tailored (trifluoroethoxy)pentafluorocyclotriphosphazene (TFPN) interacts moderately with Li+ and anions. These coordinations promote the formation of compact Li⁺-TFPN-anion nano-clusters in the electrolyte and facilitate a uniform, thin CEI during initial charging. The resulting interphase alleviates oxygen evolution and inhibits surface structural degradation, enabling the lithium-rich battery with 80% capacity retention over 1000 cycles. Furthermore, the IPAE enables a high energy density of 514 Wh kg−1 in a Li||LLO pouch cell with stable cycling. This work establishes a general design principle for high-performance electrolytes and an effective interphase engineering strategy for high-energy-density batteries with extended cycle life.

abstract: This review highlights nanosized zeolites in catalysis, emphasizing enhanced diffusion through shortened pathways and increased external surface area, which improve reactant accessibility, catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability.

title: Aqueous π‐Hole Interactions Enabled by Chiral Perfluoroarene Amphiphiles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Arene‐perfluoroarene (AP) interactions, as a representative class of π‐hole‐driven noncovalent interactions, have demonstrated unique advantages in molecular recognition and supramolecular assembly. However, the precise regulation of hydrophobic aromatic molecules in aqueous environments through AP interactions remains challenging. Herein, we designed and constructed a series of chiral perfluoroarene amphiphiles based on an octafluoronaphthalene scaffold, in which the amphiphilicity, self‐assembly behavior, and confined microenvironment were regulated through end‐group engineering, enabling selective recognition and photophysical modulation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). These perfluoroarene amphiphiles readily formed stable lamellar vesicular assemblies in aqueous solution. The π‐hole region of the perfluoroarene moiety interacted with PAHs through AP interactions, facilitating the incorporation of guest molecules into the confined lamellar domains. Consequently, a variety of hydrophobic PAHs were successfully encapsulated in aqueous media, accompanied by effective modulation of their excited‐state behaviors. Moreover, the chiral confined microenvironment induced chiroptical responses from achiral PAHs, enabling efficient chirality transfer. This work provides a new design strategy for aqueous supramolecular recognition, aromatic guest aggregation regulation, and the construction of chiral photofunctional materials based on AP interactions.

title: Single Chiroptical Pulse in Non‐Equilibrium Supramolecular Systems via Inter‐Macrocyclic Crosstalk
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Can an autonomous triphasic temporal pulse emerge in supramolecular architectures without relying on chemical transformations or external chemical fuel? Here, we demonstrate sequential chiroptical sign reversals in a time‐dependent, aperiodic circular dichroism waveform excursion governed purely by non‐covalent binding kinetics in a dual‐receptor network of pillar[5]arene and prism[5]arene. Challenging an established chiral equilibrium with an antipodal alanine derivative induces an out‐of‐equilibrium optical pulse that inverts the chiroptical sign before settling into a persistent state. This transient behavior originates from the synergy between mismatched macrocyclic binding/unbinding rates and ultra‐fast racemization of planar chirality during competitive ligand exchange, as verified by time‐resolved spectroscopy and kinetic modeling. Tailoring receptor substituents and component ratios enables straightforward regulation over both duration and amplitude of the transient response. By establishing indirect intermolecular signal relays through shared effectors, this work provides a transformative blueprint for engineering dissipative systems‐level dynamics in non‐reactive, life‐like materials.

title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantio‐ and Regioselective Addition of Silicon and Boron Nucleophiles to Methylene Cyclobutene for the Construction of Quaternary Stereocenters
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  A nickel‐catalyzed enantio‐ and regioselective addition of silicon and boron nucleophiles to the 1,3‐diene unit of methylene cyclobutenes is reported. Si─B and B─B reagents serve as silicon and boron pronucleophiles, respectively. Notably, this protocol not only constitutes the unprecedented catalytic asymmetric synthesis of cyclobutanes containing a stereogenic, silicon‐substituted quaternary carbon atom but also provides an efficient access to their boron‐substituted analogs. The transformation proceeds with excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee) and regioisomeric ratios (up to r.r. > 20:1). The substrate scope is broad, and the resulting silicon‐ and boron‐substituted products can be engaged in diverse downstream functional‐group manipulations, underscoring the synthetic utility of this methodology.

title: Intrinsic Catalyst Reactivity—not Matched Surfactant Polarity—Drives Yield Differences in Aqueous Cross‐Coupling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Micelles in aqueous–organic syntheses are commonly assumed to be the primary reaction sites that colocalize and transform reactants. However, under synthetically relevant high‐concentration conditions, including those used at scale in industrial pharmaceutical synthesis, phase separation may alter this simplified picture in poorly understood ways. Here, we investigate an aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura cross‐coupling producing a fluorescent product using triethylamine base and Kolliphor EL or Tween 80 surfactants. Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), dual‐channel imaging, and microspectroscopy reveal that micrometer‐scale triethylamine‐rich organic droplets, rather than nanoscale surfactant micelles, function as the predominant reaction sites. Direct measurements of droplet and micelle molecular compositions disprove a proposed product‐saturation inhibition mechanism based on surfactant polarity matching. Instead, the observed yield differences arise primarily from intrinsic catalyst reactivity. Surfactant‐free “on‐water” reactions further show that micelles are not required for productive coupling, supporting a primary role for surfactant in homogenization and mass transfer rather than creation of selective reaction compartments. This revised mechanistic assignment redirected reaction optimization from surfactant polarity to catalyst reactivity, affording 95% conversion to product in 20 min versus 26% under prior conditions. These findings challenge prevailing assumptions regarding micellar catalysis and demonstrate how microscale imaging can enable predictive optimization of aqueous reactions.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT

Here, we report a Bi‐based nanoalloy catalyst with atomically dispersed Cu and Mn (BiCuMn@C) for industrial‐level glycine electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical results reveal that Cu modulates the electronic structure of Bi sites via

In a membrane‐electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer, the catalyst sustains stable operation for over 1000 h with a cumulative glycine production exceeding 1 mol. This work achieves one of the best overall performances reported to date and provides practical design guidance for the industrially relevant electrosynthesis of α‐amino acids.

Highly reactive soluble halogen intermediates can facilitate the multiple electron transfer process during electrochemical reaction, but the severe shuttle behaviors and cascade corrosion would become more serious in chlorine enriched seawater electrolyte. title: Active Site Migration in Heterogeneous Hydrogenation by Coupling N‐Doped Carbon and Platinum
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  In heterogeneous hydrogenation, porous carbon supports are usually treated as passive dispersants or electronic scaffolds for metal nanoparticles. Here, we show that in specifically designed N‐doped carbon electrically coupled to Pt, the operative reduction locus can shift between catalyst components. Using p‐nitrophenol (pNP) hydrogenation as a model reaction, we decouple hydrogen activation from substrate reduction in unbiased electrochemical and thermochemical configurations. While Pt/C is required for hydrogen activation, the nitrogen‐doped TCNQ900 carbon acts as an efficient pNP reduction interface once supplied with ‐derived electrons and protons. Electrochemical measurements show that coupling to TCNQ900 displaces Pt/C from its / equilibrium along its hydrogen oxidation polarization curve, establishing a mixed‐potential‐driven electron flux toward the carbon phase. Under high ‐activation capacity, Pt‐centered (thermochemical) and carbon‐centered reductions (electrochemical) operate in parallel, increasing the overall rate. Under ‐activation‐limited conditions, electrical coupling relocates the dominant reduction locus from Pt/C to TCNQ900 with little change in total rate. We describe this reversible redistribution of catalytic function as active‐site migration. These results show that carbons can be chemically designed to serve not as passive supports, but as electronically coupled reduction interfaces that redirect hydrogenation pathways in multicomponent catalysts.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrolyte anions are generally considered passive spectators at cathodically polarized interfaces, where electrostatic exclusion and strong solvation limit their access to catalytic sites. Here we establish anion‐site coupling as a strategy to program interfacial hydration and accelerate near‐neutral electrocatalytic hydrogenation. Molecularly defined Cu
                    2+

This reconstructed hydration microenvironment accelerates proton‐coupled hydrogenation across chemically distinct substrates, enabling selective conversion of furfural to furfuryl alcohol, quinoline to tetrahydroquinoline, and nitrate to ammonia. In‐situ spectroscopy and theoretical analysis collectively reveal that anion coordination simultaneously restructures the local Cu coordination environment and interfacial water network, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier for proton‐coupled electron transfer. These findings establish coordinating anions as active molecular components of catalytic interfaces and introduce anion‐site coupling as a general strategy for programming interfacial hydration and proton‐transfer pathways in electrocatalytic synthesis.

title: Fully π‐Conjugated Nonvolatile n‐Type Additives Toward 21% Efficiency in Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Solid additive engineering represents a key strategy to modulate the morphology of organic solar cells via intermolecular interactions (van der Waals forces, hydrogen bonds, and dipole interaction) with photoactive materials. However, these weak interactions lack sufficient capacity to control the crystallization and phase separation of active layer. Here, we developed a conjugated electrostatic coupling strategy to strengthen the intermolecular forces between solid additives and donor/acceptor. The solid additive we designed possesses a fully conjugated structure that can generate strong electrostatic potential interaction, therefore a small amount of solid additive (3 wt%) facilitate ordered crystalline fibril growth of polymer donor and dense molecular packing of acceptor. In addition, the n‐type nature and nonvolatile feature of solid additive promotes the electron transport capacity and stability of the active layer. As a result, the optimal device achieved a state‐of‐the‐art efficiency of 21.02% (certificated to 20.55%), due to the prolonged exciton lifetime, suppressed charge recombination, and enhanced charge collection efficiency. This work establishes a new paradigm for solid additive engineering in organic photovoltaics.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

abstract:
ABSTRACT

title: Gating Oxygen Flux in High‐Nickel Layered Cathodes via a Surface‐Bulk Oxygen‐Fixation Framework
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐Ni layered oxide cathodes suffer from severe high‐voltage degradation driven by oxygen‐vacancy evolution, lattice oxygen release, and interfacial reconstruction. Here, a LaCeNb

The modified cathode establishes a spatial oxygen‐fixation‐gate framework, integrating bulk oxygen locking by Nb, surface oxygen retention by La/Ce, and interfacial oxygen buffering by the oxygen‐vacancy‐rich layer. STEM, depth‐resolved XPS, XAS, DEMS, EPR, in situ XRD, and DFT calculations reveal that this coupled regulation stabilizes both oxygen chemistry and structural evolution. title: Investigation of Structure‐Property‐Performance Relationships of Binders in Graphitic Negative Electrodes for Lithium Ion Batteries on the Example of Systematically Modified Xanthan
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  This study investigates structure‐property‐performance relationships of xanthan‐based biopolymer binders in graphitic negative electrodes in lithium‐ion batteries. Xanthan gum (XG) variants possess well‐defined molecular structures and stable shear‐thinning behavior, which makes them ideal for systematic investigations. The influence of side chain composition, degree of acetylation and/or pyruvylation, and polymer molecular weight is investigated on electrode and paste properties (i.e., adhesion, conductivity, rheology, and electrochemical performance). A higher degree of acetylation enhances adhesion through improved interaction with the non‐polar copper current collector, while other properties remain unaffected. In contrast, a pyruvyl group reduces adhesion and conductivity due to poor compatibility with non‐polar components, promoting carbon‐binder heterogeneity. Larger side groups hinder adhesion and thixotropy (paste relaxation) as steric effects restrict polymer flexibility and prolong paste relaxation. Higher polymer molecular weight improves shear‐thinning behavior and thixotropy, minimizing sedimentation and edge effects, though slightly decreasing conductivity. Overall, these results establish clear correlations between the molecular structure of (XG‐based) biopolymer binders and electrode performance. The insights provide design guidelines for optimizing binder composition to balance rheological control, adhesion, and conductivity, contributing to more efficient electrode processing and improved performance in next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries.

title: 4 V‐Class Calcium‐Based Water‐in‐Salt Electrolyte for Aqueous Calcium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    We report the first systematic investigation and demonstration of calcium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (Ca(TFSI)
                    2

                    2

Spectroscopic characterization combined with molecular simulations reveals a distinctive solvation structure in which Ca
                    2+

                    2

                    −

Extensive ion association is also evident through solvent‐shared ion pairs, consistent with suppressed water activity and an expanded ESW. Furthermore, the addition of a small amount of acetonitrile enables the electrolyte to remain liquid at sub‐zero temperatures, while lowering viscosity and enhancing ionic conductivity without substantially disrupting the Ca
                    2+

Leveraging these electrolyte properties, full cells employing perylene‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic diimide or Sn anodes and a Prussian blue analogue cathode demonstrate robust electrochemical performance at −20°C, including operation over a 3.2 V window with the Sn‐based cell, with long‐term cycling stability and sub‐zero device operation. These findings establish Ca(TFSI)

title: Multiscale Engineering of Three‐Phase Interfaces for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) offer high efficiency and zero‐emission operation, yet membrane electrode assembly performance is constrained by coupled oxygen, proton, electron, and water transport. This review summarizes advances in multiscale three‐phase interface engineering. At the nanoscale, catalyst protection, catalyst–ionomer interactions, molecular modifiers, and ionomer design improve active site accessibility and oxygen transport. At the electrode scale, support microenvironments and catalyst layer architectures regulate pore connectivity, wettability, ionomer distribution, electronic conduction, and water removal. At the device scale, structured assemblies, membranes, gas diffusion layers, microporous layers, and flow fields coordinate mass and charge transport under practical conditions. Future priorities include scalable fabrication, operando diagnostics, multiscale modeling, and AI‐assisted optimization. By integrating interfacial, electrode, and device engineering, this review provides a framework for developing durable, high‐power, low‐platinum PEMFCs and advancing automotive fuel cell stacks with improved performance, lifetime, and economic feasibility.

title: A Perspective on Hydrothermal Catalysis for Chemical Recycling of Polyolefin‐Rich Plastic Waste
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Polyolefins dominate global plastic production, yet most post‐consumer polyolefin waste is too mixed, wet, or contaminated for mechanical recycling. Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) converts such waste in hot, compressed water into hydrocarbon oils compatible with existing refineries and steam crackers, without pre‐drying. Water under hydrothermal conditions acts as a heat transfer medium, pseudo‐organic solvent, ionic catalyst, and purification phase, suppressing char and aromatics while partitioning heteroatoms into the aqueous phase. However, polyolefin degradation in hot water still proceeds through unselective radical scission, producing broad, waxy product distributions. This Perspective identifies catalysis as the key to achieving selective and scalable chemical recycling of polyolefins by HTL. Hydrothermal catalysis is distinct from catalytic pyrolysis, as water alters acid‐site chemistry, interfacial reactivity, and hydrogen availability while accelerating zeolite dealumination, support dissolution, and metal sintering. Catalyst design principles are discussed, including acid, metal, and bifunctional sites for selective chain scission and strategies for hydrothermal stability. Process integration of HTL oil with steam cracking, fluid catalytic cracking, and gasification is assessed, together with techno–economic and policy factors favoring olefins over fuels. Finally, research priorities are outlined, including long‐duration catalyst testing, mechanistic studies in hot compressed water, reactor scale‐up, and coupled techno–economic and life cycle assessment.

title: Injectable Self‐Healing Microspheres Enable In Situ Assembly of Dynamic Porous Scaffolds for Tissue Repair
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Tissue engineering scaffolds are indispensable for repairing complex tissue defects; however, conventional prefabricated scaffolds are limited by invasive implantation, poor anatomical conformity, and insufficient adaptability to irregular defect geometries. Here, we report an injectable, self‐assembling scaffold strategy that transforms polymer microspheres from isolated functional carriers into dynamic modular building blocks for in situ scaffold construction. Following injection, the self‐healing microspheres fill irregular defects, fuse with adjacent microspheres, and form a mechanically stable three‐dimensional scaffold with an interconnected porous architecture. This design combines the minimally invasive delivery and functional versatility of microspheres with the structural integrity and mechanical support of macroscopic scaffolds, thereby addressing a key challenge in precise and conformal tissue repair. The platform also enables disease‐specific functionalization through metal‐ion coordination. Silver‐ion‐loaded microspheres provide conformal coverage of complex wounds while exhibiting antibacterial activity and supporting skin regeneration. Zinc‐ion‐functionalized microspheres assemble into defect‐matched porous scaffolds and promote osteogenic repair. Copper‐ion‐integrated microspheres remain localized at tumor sites and provide sustained release of therapeutic agents, thereby reducing systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work establishes a minimally invasive, shape‐adaptive, and customizable scaffold platform for complex tissue repair and localized therapy. More broadly, it provides a versatile design framework for the development of next‐generation intelligent biomaterials.

title: Charge Escape Mechanism and Lifetime Prediction of Non‐Contact Triboelectric Sensors
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Non‐contact triboelectric sensors (NC‐TES) have attracted considerable attention for high‐frequency motion monitoring. However, their service life is fundamentally limited by the inevitable dissipation of surface charges. In this study, surface charges are categorized into retention and escape charges according to their escape behavior. Three charge escape mechanisms are systematically elucidated based on the electron trap energy distribution theory. On this basis, a general mathematical model is established to quantitatively characterize charge escape, enabling reliable prediction of the service life of NC‐TES. The influences of the intermediate layer, air gap of stator‐rotor, and humidity on the charge escape rate are investigated, providing design guidelines for improving sensor durability. Durability tests are performed on ten dielectric materials, among which fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) exhibits an expected lifetime of up to 8940 h at 100 Hz. Furthermore, the charge escape behavior of NC‐TES under various operating conditions is experimentally evaluated. The excellent agreement between the experimental results and theoretical predictions validates the proposed model, enabling accurate lifetime estimation and design optimization for specific operating conditions. This work establishes a theoretical framework for the design and lifetime prediction of NC‐TES, thereby facilitating the deployment of self‐powered sensing in industrial applications.

title: Size‐Dependent Photoelectric and Photothermal Effects in Plasmon‐Induced Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Plasmonic photocatalysis relies on the conversion of photon energy into nonequilibrium charge carriers and heat. However, the relative contributions of these processes and their size‐dependent roles in photocatalysis remain unclear because of their intrinsically intertwined nature. Here, size‐controlled Ag NPs/p‐GaN heterostructures are employed to quantitatively disentangle the size‐dependent roles of hot‐electron injection and surface heating in determining photocatalytic activity. Analysis of the size‐dependent hydrogen evolution reaction activity shows that the apparent contribution of localized heating is strongly dependent on Ag NP size, accounting for less than 10% of the overall activity in smaller particles (< 28 nm) but increasing to nearly 50% in larger particles. Spatially resolved SPV imaging reveals enhanced charge separation with increasing Ag NP size, while ultrafast spectroscopy shows elevated electron temperatures and prolonged electron‐phonon coupling dynamics. By combining spatially and temporally resolved techniques, we observe a correlation between the systematic evolution of local charge density and hot‐carrier relaxation dynamics with particle size while identifying an important role of heat in the enhancement. These results identify plasmonic nanoparticle size as a critical determinant of the photocatalytic mechanism, offering a mechanistic framework for selectively routing solar energy into targeted photocatalytic pathways.

title: Reaction‐Pathway Regulation for Degradation‐Insensitive Direct Regeneration of Spent LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 Cathode Materials
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Direct regeneration is limited by degradation‐dependent processing because cathodes with different degradation states cannot be regenerated using a uniform protocol. Using LiNi
                    0.5
                    Co
                    0.2
                    Mn
                    0.3
                    O
                    2
                    (NCM523) cathode materials with different degradation states, we show that this limitation originates from competition among relithiation, structural recovery, and thermal decomposition during calcination. As the balance of these competing reactions shifts with degradation state, cathodes evolve along distinct reaction trajectories. Recognizing that these reactions are governed by the reactants, we regulate the regeneration reaction through the lithium‐source reactant, causing cathode materials with different degradation states to pass through the same type of low‐symmetry, synthesis‐derived intermediate structure during calcination. This redirects regeneration toward a reconstruction pathway with favorable thermodynamics and improved ion diffusion, enabling rapid Li replenishment, long‐range cation ordering, and structural restoration. Consequently, practical NCM523 black mass is regenerated into cathodes that deliver higher capacity and better capacity retention than those regenerated via the conventional pathway, and a 1.3 Ah pouch cell with the regenerated cathode retains 80.2% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles. This reconstruction pathway also enables direct upcycling of degraded NCM523 toward higher‐Ni compositions. Broadly, this work provides a mechanistic framework for reducing degradation‐state dependence in direct regeneration of spent cathode materials.

title: Tuning σ‐Type Ni─O Orbital Hybridization for Stable Ultrahigh‐Ni Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ultrahigh‐Ni layered oxides have emerged as leading candidates for next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), yet they suffer from severe chemo‐mechanical degradation driven by irreversible lattice oxygen loss during cycling. In this study, we propose an orbital hybridization regulation strategy via co‐doping high‐electronegativity cations (M = Zr
                    4+
                    /Ta
                    5+
                    /W
                    6+
                    ) to stabilize lattice oxygen and improve redox reversibility. Combined structural and theoretical analyses reveal that co‐doping induces electron redistribution around oxygen atoms, thereby weakening
                    σ
                    ‐type Ni–O hybridization and suppressing irreversible ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer and oxygen vacancy formation. Concurrently, the enhanced covalency of M─O bonds facilitates electron delocalization for charge compensation that reduces highly oxidized nickel species in the charged state. This stabilized redox chemistry mitigates transition metal (TM) migration, lattice distortion, and crack propagation. Additionally, elemental co‐doping also induces a lattice‐coherent rock‐salt surface layer that effectively suppresses interfacial parasitic reactions. The co‐doped cathode delivers exceptional cycling stability, with nearly 100% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 1 C (2.7–4.3 V) in half cells, and 93.5% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C (2.8–4.2 V) in pouch cells. This study provides an alternative avenue for stable ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes from the perspective of local chemistry and orbital hybridization modulation.

title: Coupling Macrophage Reeducation With Mechanical Remodeling of the Tumor Extracellular Matrix to Enhance Pancreatic Cancer Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    One major challenge in reeducating macrophages lies in the specific delivery of therapeutic agents to these cells. Here we report a multi‐arm polymer conjugate of the toll‐like receptor 7/8 agonist resiquimod and soy protein (mPDPC‐RS) that simultaneously dismantles the immune and physical barriers within pancreatic tumors. Upon systemic administration, mPDPC‐RS preferentially accumulates in tumor‐associated macrophages in vivo, repolarizes them toward an antitumor phenotype, and thereby initiates robust immune responses. Concurrently, mPDPC‐RS reduces interstitial fluid pressure and solid stress of the tumor as well as tumor stiffness, thereby facilitating CD8
                    +
                    T cell infiltration. In murine pancreatic cancer models, this dual‐function platform produces profound tumor suppression and markedly extends survival. Our findings provide a versatile platform with high macrophage avidity for cancer immunotherapy and establish a comprehensive strategy for overcoming both biological and mechanical defenses of the tumor microenvironment to improve immunotherapeutic outcomes in pancreatic cancer.

title: Interploidy massively increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Meiotic recombination reshuffles genetic diversity through reciprocal DNA exchanges between chromosomes known as crossovers. In most eukaryotes, crossovers are highly constrained in both frequency and distribution, leaving large genomic regions with little or no recombination. A notable exception is the
                    Brassica
                    AAC allotriploid hybrid obtained from a cross between allotetraploid
                    Brassica napus
                    (AACC) and diploid
                    Brassica rapa
                    (AA), which exhibits elevated recombination and crossover formation near centromeres. Here, we generated a CCA allotriploid hybrid from a cross between
                    B. napus
                    and
                    Brassica oleracea
                    (CC), and subsequently produced AAC allotriploids by crossing the CCA hybrid with
                    B. rapa
                    . Both CCA and AAC allotriploids exhibit similar meiotic deregulation, demonstrating that this phenomenon is not restricted to AAC hybrids. Both systems displayed a marked increase in crossover frequency within normally low-recombining chromosome regions, reaching 9.4-fold in AAC and 13.4-fold in CCA allotriploids. Alternating CCA and AAC allotriploids efficiently reshuffled both
                    B. napus
                    subgenomes within only two generations. Using genetic mapping and cytogenetics, we further identified homoeologous exchanges. Remarkably, crossovers occurring on chromosomes involved in homoeologous associations exhibited a more pronounced redistribution toward nonrecombining regions than those on homologously paired chromosomes. Moreover, the frequency of homoeologous associations varied with the diploid progenitor genotype, indicating that genetic factors controlling homoeologous recombination already exist in
                    Brassica
                    diploids. Altogether, our results identify allotriploidy as a simple and powerful strategy to unlock recombination deserts, which harbor 21% of total resistance gene analogs, and provide insights into its potential role in allopolyploid evolution, adaptation, and speciation.

title: Gap test–inspired crack-parallel tension tests of fracture of soft-knitted polymer composites simulated by microplane triads
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Soft composites are increasingly used in wearable and soft robotic systems, as advances in material architecture enable greater damage tolerance under large deformation. In these mesoscale architectures, the crack-parallel stresses modify the crack initiation and growth in the opening-mode fracture. Emulating the gap test, we introduce a fracture test to quantify how the superposed crack-parallel tension affects the maximum load (i.e., the load capacity) and the load-deflection curve. A Mode I (opening mode) center-notched tensioned strip is used because its advantages in generating crack-parallel tension outweigh its hypothetical disadvantages with possible instability of crack jumps at two competing crack fronts. We develop and experimentally validate a continuum model that captures the nonlinear behavior and progressive damage of knitted composites. To this end, we introduce an ensemble of oriented microplane triads tangential to the yarn at characteristic points of the yarn loop within a repetitive unit cell of the knit. The triads ensure the yarn-polymer transfer of all normal and shear stress components at each characteristic point. The experimentally calibrated computational model provides a tool to predict the effect of crack-parallel tension on the changes of load capacity and of the effective fracture energy of knitted polymer composites, enabling rational design of these composites in engineering applications such as wearables and soft robotics.

title: Soil contamination and acidification jointly increased cereal cadmium and dietary exposure over four decades
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Cadmium contamination of staple cereals is an important food-safety concern, yet how long-term changes in soil chemistry alter cadmium transfer into food remains poorly resolved. Here we reconstructed changes in cropland topsoil cadmium and pH across China from 1980 to 2020 and quantified their consequences for cereal grain cadmium, dietary exposure, and mitigation potential. National mean topsoil cadmium increased from 0.123 to 0.236 mg kg
                    −1
                    , while mean cropland pH declined from 6.50 to 6.30 nationally and by about 0.5 units in several southern rice-growing provinces. These coupled changes increased mean grain cadmium from 0.043 to 0.100 mg kg
                    −1
                    in rice and from 0.017 to 0.032 mg kg
                    −1
                    in wheat. By 2020, provinces with estimated mean hazard quotients exceeded 1.0 had a combined population of about 138 million. Counterfactual analysis showed that soil cadmium accumulation remained the dominant driver of rising grain cadmium, while acidification substantially amplified soil-to-grain transfer, especially in rice systems. Scenario analysis to 2050 indicated that restoring cropland pH to 6.5 could offset about 44% of the projected increase in rice cadmium even without immediate source control, whereas combining pH restoration with source control reduced mean rice cadmium by about 59% and brought exceedance close to zero. These findings identify soil acidification as an important amplifier of cadmium transfer into staple cereals and highlight targeted cropland pH restoration as a practical near-term strategy for reducing food-chain exposure while longer-term source-control measures take effect.

title: Targeted metabolic reprogramming of CD8 T cells restores immune regulation in lupus
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by pathogenic humoral autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking T cell dysfunction to aberrant B cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a CD8
                    +
                    T cell–intrinsic metabolic defect that promotes humoral immune dysregulation in lupus. CD8
                    +
                    T cells from patients with SLE exhibited elevated CD38 expression associated with reduced intracellular NAD
                    +
                    levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cytotoxic capacity. Pharmacologic inhibition of CD38 with the small-molecule inhibitor MK-0159 restored NAD
                    +
                    metabolism and rescued cytotoxic function in human CD8
                    +
                    T cells ex vivo. To selectively target this pathway in vivo, we developed anti-CD8 antibody-conjugated nanoparticles encapsulating MK-0159. In lupus-prone MRL/
                    lpr
                    mice, CD8-targeted delivery enhanced granzyme B expression, improved degranulation, reduced plasmablast responses and autoantibody production, immune complex deposition, and renal pathology. Importantly, targeted delivery restored CD8
                    +
                    T cell function without broad immune perturbation. These findings identify CD38-driven NAD
                    +
                    depletion as a reversible immunometabolic checkpoint limiting CD8
                    +
