title: Age-associated B cells drive lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in Faslpr mice through the p38α−CXCL10 signaling axis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Defective Fas cell surface death receptor (FAS) signaling leads to lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder, yet the mechanisms involved remain unclear. Using genetic mouse models homozygous for the lymphoproliferation spontaneous mutation (
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    ), we showed that age-associated B cells (ABCs) were critical drivers of lymphadenopathy and autoimmunity. Single-cell transcriptomics of lymph node immune cells in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice revealed a marked expansion of ABCs. Depletion of these ABCs in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice significantly restrained lymph node enlargement and alleviated autoimmune manifestations, whereas adoptive transfer of ABCs from
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice to wild-type mice exacerbated disease pathology. Mechanistically, p38α signaling emerged as a critical regulator of ABC differentiation and function, and conditional deletion of p38α in CD11c
                    +
                    cells profoundly suppressed ABC expansion and ameliorated autoimmune manifestations in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice. Furthermore, we identified CXCL10 as an important downstream effector of p38α signaling in ABCs that drives autoimmune disorder. Neutralization of CXCL10 significantly attenuated disease severity in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice. Although clinical relevance analyses of autoimmune patient cohorts revealed a parallel expansion of ABCs in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and primary Sjögren’s syndrome, ABCs with higher p38α content were specifically enriched in SLE patients. Together, these findings identify p38α-driven ABCs as an important regulator of lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice and suggest that targeting the p38α−CXCL10 axis in ABCs may be a therapeutic strategy for treating this autoimmune disease.

title: A sweeping twist defect as a topological flagellum that enhances colloid translation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Nematic liquid crystals can dramatically reconfigure under dynamic forcing, providing exciting opportunities in active matter. Here, we study a disk colloid with hybrid planar and homeotropic anchoring rotated by an external magnetic field which generates a dynamic companion topological defect. The disk moves faster when the defect sweeps across the disk’s face. We identify the defect as a nonsingular twist wall, characterize the twist energy landscape, and identify that the sweeping motion is driven by a topological instability. As the defect sweeps, it reverses the handedness of twist and lowers the free energy in the fluid in the gap above the disk. Landau–de Gennes modeling shows that the sweeping wall behaves as a propagating director texture: the director field is nearly stationary in the wall frame, while nematogens rotate locally as the wall passes. The nematogens’ rotation generates a viscous stress on the surface of the disk that hastens its propulsion. Thus, the defect acts as a flagellum that powers colloid swimming, providing an example of a dissipative topological structure whose dynamics can be harnessed to perform useful work.

title: Mechanical instability generates monodisperse colloidosomes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Formation and rupture of vesicles are fundamental processes underlying diverse phenomena in biology, materials science, and biomedical applications. Vesicles form when the area of a growing disk-like membrane reaches the instability point at which the energy barrier to the disk-to-vesicle transition vanishes. Observing such topological transitions in lipid bilayers is a challenge because of their nanoscale dimensions and rapid dynamics. We study a scaled-up model of membranes assembled from rod-shaped colloidal particles. The unique features of colloidal membranes enable the real-time visualization of spontaneous vesicle closure driven by an instability arising from competition between edge and bending energies that is universal to all membrane-based materials. A continuum theory with independently measured material parameters quantitatively predicts the instability point for vesicle formation and intermediate membrane conformations during the disk-to-vesicle transition. The instability generates monodisperse, selectively permeable colloidosomes whose size is controlled by gravity and membrane elasticity, providing a scalable and programmable platform for diverse applications.

title: Modulating chain conformations and hydrogen-bond dynamics at silica–rubber interfaces for enhanced energy dissipation in composites
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The polymer–nanoparticle interphase is essential for fabricating high-performance nanocomposites, as it dictates mechanical properties through interfacial stress transfer and energy dissipation. However, engineering the buried interphases remains challenging due to the complex hierarchical structure and methodological limitations, particularly in silica–rubber systems where confined polymer chain conformation and hydrogen-bond dynamics are poorly resolved. Herein, a selective polymer-removal technique was developed to strip free and loosely bound polymer under extreme conditions, enabling TEM visualization of polymer chain-like interfacial features consistent with train-, loop-, and tail-like adsorption motifs in silica/silicone rubber nanocomposites. Correlative analysis combining STEM-EELS, high-resolution NMR, in situ variable-temperature IR, and 2D low-field NMR spectroscopy resolves hydrogen bonding between silica surface hydroxyls and silicone backbone oxygen atoms (Si-O-H···O-Si), which exhibit temperature-dependent behavior. Quantitative analysis reveals the strategic modulation of interphase layer thickness: As the apparent hydroxyl density of silica varied from 2.1 to 12.9 OH nm
                    −2
                    , the interphase thickness increased from 4.1 ± 0.8 nm to 13.2 ± 1.4 nm (9.5 mol% polymer phenyl); increasing the polymer phenyl content to 29.7 mol% further expands the layer to 23.4 ± 1.0 nm. Molecular dynamics simulations also suggest that higher silica surface hydroxyl density enhances multipoint adsorption of polymer chain, which promotes the formation of loop and train conformations. These confined chain arrangements are consistent with the reduced Arrhenius activation energy from 101 to 50 kJ mol
                    −1
                    measured by dynamic rheology, which facilitates interfacial chain mobility and hydrogen-bond exchange during deformation. These findings provide molecular-level insights for the rational design of polymer nanocomposites.

title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus
                    Orthopneumovirus
                    ) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the
                    SH
                    viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

title: Pinning of Van Hove singularities and correlated insulators in M-valley twisted transition metal dichalcogenides
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We investigate the role of long-range Coulomb interactions in M-valley moirés using the self-consistent Hartree–Fock approximation. This platform was recently proposed [D. Călugăru et al.,
                    Nature
                    643
                    , 376–381 (2025) and C. Lei
                    et al., Phys. Rev. Lett.
                    135
                    , 196402 (2025)] as a new class of experimentally realizable moiré materials using twisted transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) homobilayers with the 1T structure. While these seminal studies considered the noninteracting theory without an electric displacement field, this work shows that both electron–electron interactions at finite doping and an interlayer bias strongly modify the moiré bands. For small twists (
                    
                      
                        ≲
                      
                    
                    5°) the density of states versus filling and interlayer bias displays qualitatively different behavior for twisting near aligned (0°) and antialigned (60°) stacking with tunable Van Hove singularities (VHSs). Moreover, interactions pin the VHS to the Fermi energy over a finite range of doping both at zero and finite bias depending on the stacking type, an effect known to enhance both superconductivity and strongly correlated states. At half-filling, we obtain the phase diagram as a function of interaction strength, interlayer bias, and twist angle. We find a competition driven by band mixing between an isotropic ferromagnet and an antiferromagnet that are nearly degenerate over a wide range of experimentally accessible parameters. Our work demonstrates that correlated states in M-valley twisted TMD homobilayers can be strongly tuned in situ both by applying an electric displacement field and by electron doping.

title: Ion‐Pair Mediation Enables Low‐Viscosity, Nonflammable Ternary Hybrid Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have garnered attention as promising energy storage devices owing to their intrinsic safety. However, the practical energy density of AZMBs is severely constrained by the narrow electrochemical window and sluggish kinetics inherent to conventional concentrated or viscous aqueous electrolytes. To address these limitations, a ternary hybrid system comprising a Zn(OTf)
                    2
                    /LiOTf dual‐salt matrix and low‐volume (5 vol.%) 1‐ethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (EMIMTFSI, abbreviated as EMT) ionic liquid is constructed. In the ternary system, EMIM
                    +

                    −
                    /OTf

More importantly, these ion pairs undergo adsorption‐reduction‐anchoring to form an inner inorganic/outer organic bilayer, where OTf
                    −
                    /TFSI
                    −

                    +

                    −2

                    2

                    −1

                    2

title: Ion‐Pair Decoupler Tunes Solvation Chemistry for Room‐Temperature Polymer Electrolytes With Built‐In Flame Retardancy
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solid‐state polymer electrolytes for high‐energy lithium‐metal batteries are severely constrained by low room‐temperature ionic conductivity. However, mainstream approaches focus on regulating the aggregate structure and flexibility of polymer chains while neglecting the ionic solvation microenvironment, which caps ionic conductivity gains at a marginal level. Here, an innovative ion‐pair decoupling strategy is proposed to reshape the Li
                    +
                    solvation chemistry within polymer matrices and to facilitate rapid ionic conduction. The ion‐pair decoupler, diethyl phosphoramidate, promotes the dissociation of lithium salt into a configuration dominated by solvent‐separated ion pairs by coordinating with Li
                    +
                    via its electron‐rich P = O groups and anchoring TFSI
                    ‒
                    through hydrogen bond donors. Consequently, the ionic conductivity of the engineered electrolyte increases 24.6‐fold at 25°C. Li symmetric cells achieve stable cycling over 850 h, and Li||LiFePO
                    4
                    cells deliver a high‐capacity retention rate of 96.5% after 400 cycles at 25°C. Furthermore, the designed electrolyte exhibits excellent self‐extinguishing flame‐retardant properties by combining gas‐phase radical scavenging and condensed‐phase char‐forming mechanisms. Thus, a single molecular design simultaneously serves as an ion‐pair decoupler and an intrinsic flame retardant, establishing solvation‐chemistry tuning as a new paradigm for safe, room‐temperature solid polymer electrolytes.

source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sodium metal batteries (SMBs) are promising candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage systems, yet their practical application is hindered by dendritic growth and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation. Herein, we report an in situ interfacial regulation strategy by introducing amorphous SiO
                    2
                    (a‑SiO
                    2

This synergetic inorganic‐rich SEI homogenizes Na deposition and accelerates ion diffusion kinetics. As a result, the Na/a‑SiO

title: Unified Grain‐Boundary and Electrode‐Interface Engineering Enables High‐Performance Magnesium‐Based Thermoelectrics
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐performance thermoelectric devices require not only intrinsically efficient materials but also minimized transport losses across multiple interfaces during device integration. However, internal transport interfaces and external electrode contacts are typically optimized independently, creating a persistent challenge in translating material‐level advances into device‐level performance. Here we establish a unified interface engineering strategy in Bi‐rich Mg
                    3
                    (Sb,Bi)
                    2

                    Sb

                    Bi

First‐principles calculations and atomic‐scale characterization reveal that the Bi‐rich composition suppresses extensive Nb‐related reactions while enabling electronically favorable confined interfaces. Nb incorporation increases the weighted mobility to 315.6 cm

title: In Situ Polymerized Interfaces Enable Robust and High‐Performance Dry‐Coating Electrodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Dry‐coating electrode technology eliminates the use of toxic N‐methyl‐2‐pyrrolidone and offers a promising route for sustainable battery manufacturing. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the weak interfacial mechanics among rigid cathode particles, polytetrafluoroethylene nanofibers, and conductive carbon additives. These fragile interfaces reduce mechanical robustness and interfacial stability, thereby compromising both processability and electrochemical performance. Here, we report an in situ polymerization strategy using a polymerizable deep eutectic liquid additive, which forms an adhesive polymer network upon photopolymerization, thereby reinforcing contact among electrode components and improving electrode robustness. The resulting dry‐coating LiNi
                    0.8
                    Co
                    0.1
                    Mn
                    0.1

title: Coupled hydrogen spillover and CO2 activation sites in high-entropy catalysts for CO2 reduction
source: Chem
abstract: Converting CO2 into useful chemicals via reverse water-gas shift reaction offers a promising route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, catalysts often struggle to coordinate hydrogen and CO2 activation while remaining stable under demanding reaction conditions. The present work developed high-entropy oxides with Li and Al dual-atom doping to promote cooperative alloy-oxide interfaces with coupled H2 and CO2 activation sites, thereby enabling fast, selective, and stable CO production. These findings provide a general strategy for integrating multiple functions into robust catalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Comprehensive synthesis of K48/K63 ubiquitin pentamers by graph-empowered automation
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Linear, branched and heterotypic ubiquitin (Ub) chains regulate essential cellular processes, yet their structural and functional analysis remains limited by the difficulty of preparing defined, homogeneous samples. Here we establish a fully automated platform for the comprehensive synthesis of all 56 K48/K63-linked Ub tetramers and pentamers, by iterative cycles of K48- or K63-specific chemoenzymatic conjugations of chemically synthesized Ub monomers bearing a fast-cleaving lysine protecting group compatible with folded proteins. A graph-based digital encoding of Ub chain topologies enabled systematic enumeration and filtering of reaction pathways, guiding the selection of synthetic routes. This computational system generates reagent maps and executable code to direct iterative deprotection and conjugation cycles on a standard, laboratory liquid-handling robot. All 14 Ub tetramers and 42 Ub pentamers were obtained with high fidelity, as validated by SDS–PAGE and mass spectrometry. This work establishes a general framework for automated protein conjugate synthesis and provides access to the complete space of K48/K63 branched ubiquitin chains.

title: Learning beyond rigid manipulation with hybrid soft-rigid robots
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Rigid-soft robot hybrids promise to unite the precision and repeatability of rigid manipulators with the compliance and adaptability of soft structures. Yet, full-fledged rigid-soft manipulators remain largely unexplored, in part because the intelligence required to exploit this combination is still missing. Here, we introduce a hybrid robotic system obtained by the series interconnection of a rigid arm and a soft manipulator, and systematically examine its ability to perform both established and previously inaccessible manipulation tasks. We show that a tailored imitation learning algorithm–generally applicable to this class of hybrid systems–leverages the complementary roles of rigid precision and soft embodiment to acquire manipulation skills and generalize them in a single shot across task variations. As a result, the system matches or exceeds the performance of rigid robots in classical tasks such as stacking, while enabling qualitatively new behaviors, including grasping objects through narrow openings.

title: Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing
source: Nature Materials
abstract: The dynamic behaviour of diffusive memristors enables bio-realistic emulation of artificial neurons and synapses, yet scaling from individual devices to neuromorphic systems remains challenging. Stochasticity in ionic motion and filament evolution limits both the uniformity and tunability of these devices, hindering reliable system-level implementation. Here we present a framework for tailoring the relaxation dynamics of diffusive memristors via intrinsic and extrinsic tuning. Percolation in a thin platinum interfacial layer and grain boundaries in a polycrystalline hafnium oxide matrix spatially confine active metal-ion migration; this guided transport substantially improves device uniformity. Purpose-designed programming protocols enable tuning of relaxation time over two orders of magnitude. A prototype hardware system integrating a 28 × 14 array of tailored diffusive memristors and a memristive system-on-chip implements the hierarchy-of-time-surfaces algorithm, achieving 91.14% recognition accuracy on a downsampled neuromorphic-MNIST dataset. These results demonstrate a scalable approach towards robust and energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware for next-generation artificial intelligence.

title: Tailorable deep eutectic solvents for sustainable lignocellulose refining: from platform design to value-added products
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Efficient utilization of renewable carbon requires lignocellulosic biorefineries that can deconstruct plant cell walls while preserving the value of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), constructed from programmable hydrogen-bond acceptors and donors, have emerged as tunable media for lignocellulose processing. This review discusses recent progress in the rational design of DESs for lignocellulosic biorefineries, focusing on binary, ternary, hydrated, biphasic, catalytic and biocompatible systems. By regulating acidity/basicity, polarity, hydrogen-bonding ability, viscosity, water tolerance, active sites and phase behavior, DESs can selectively disrupt lignin-carbohydrate complexes, stabilize or functionalize the components, and direct the downstream transformation of the components toward bio-based chemicals and functional polymeric materials. Component-oriented valorization routes are summarized, including cellulose-derived functional materials and platform chemicals, lignin-derived aromatics and functional polymers, and hemicellulose-derived furan chemicals. Key barriers to industrial deployment are also critically examined, including high viscosity, mass-transfer limitations, solvent loss, energy-intensive recovery, feedstock heterogeneity, incomplete mechanistic understanding and insufficient techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Future opportunities are highlighted in artificial-intelligence-guided DESs discovery, novel membrane and electrodialysis DES-recovery technologies, DES-compatible chemo-biocatalysis and closed-loop process integration. Tailorable DESs are expected to evolve from empirical solvent systems into predictive, recyclable and product-oriented platforms for sustainable production of bio-based chemicals, materials and fuels.

title: Dominant role of Southeast Asian emissions in anthropogenic increases in global tropospheric ozone and southward tropical growth, 2000–2019
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Widespread increases in tropospheric ozone (O3) have been reported over the past two decades, with changes in anthropogenic emissions, particularly in Asia, identified as an important driver. Here we use global model sensitivity simulations to quantify changes in global tropospheric O3 burden and associated radiative forcing (RF) attributable to anthropogenic emission changes from 2000 to 2019, and assess the contributions from different Asian regions. Changes in anthropogenic emissions increased the global tropospheric O3 burden by 12.0 ± 0.5 Tg and global mean RF by 0.030 ± 0.002 W m–2 under fixed 2015–2019 meteorological fields. The increase was larger during 2000–2010 than during 2010–2019 and occurred predominantly in the tropics. Southeast Asia was the largest regional contributor over 2000–2019, accounting for 5.7 ± 0.4 Tg of the simulated global tropospheric O3 burden increase and 0.020 ± 0.002 W m–2 of RF. During 2010–2019, the increase in tropospheric O3 burden attributable to anthropogenic emission changes was larger over 0–30°S than over 0–30°N, indicating a southward shift in the tropical response driven primarily by Southeast Asian emissions. East Asia shifted from a major positive contributor during 2000–2010 to a negative contributor during 2010–2019. These results highlight the increasing importance of anthropogenic emissions from tropical Asia in shaping the global distribution of tropospheric O3 and its climate forcing.

title: Chemical defects in semiconducting polymers and their impact on reproducibility and device performance
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Conjugated polymers are central to the field of organic electronics. The continuous drive to develop high-performance materials and explore alternative synthetic routes has led to unprecedented chemical versatility, allowing researchers to finely tune semiconducting polymer properties for specific applications. However, non-optimal polymerization conditions and/or limited differentiation between reacting monomers may facilitate side reactions, leading to the covalent incorporation of structural defects. Depending on their nature, these defects can perturb the electronic structure of conjugated polymers, causing varying degrees of deviation from the envisioned structure. As a result, structure–property relationships depend not only on molar mass, molar mass distribution and end groups but also on defect level. In this Perspective, we discuss these structural discrepancies and encourage researchers to critically evaluate the polymers they synthesize and study, recognizing structural variability as a potential driver of batch-to-batch inconsistency. We illustrate the origins of structural defects, outline strategies to limit or avoid them, and assess commonly used characterization techniques. Furthermore, we showcase the influence of structural irregularities on physicochemical and optoelectronic material properties, as well as device performance. Finally, we explore how structural defects can present opportunities, potentially offering new perspectives for materials design.

title: Full‐Process Synergistic Optimization of Buried Interfaces via Molecule‐Assisted Co‐Assembly for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are promising hole‐selective contacts for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet insufficient substrate anchoring and weak buried‐interface interactions limit device efficiency and stability. Here, we report a co‐assembled SAM (Co‐SAM) strategy that enables full‐process synergistic optimization of the perovskite buried interface by introducing tris(4‐fluorophenyl)phosphine oxide (TFPPO) into SAMs. TFPPO suppresses SAM aggregation in solution via its strongly polar P═O group and anchors onto NiO
                    x
                    , with its 4‐fluorophenyl arms proposed to interact with unanchored hydroxyl groups of SAMs to strengthen anchoring and refine their arrangement. Furthermore, TFPPO optimizes the interfacial chemical states while serving as an effective template to direct high‐quality perovskite crystal growth. Consequently, inverted PSCs based on the regulated SAMs achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 26.98% (stabilized PCE of 26.40%) and 20.65% for normal‐bandgap (1.54 eV) and wide‐bandgap (1.78 eV) devices, respectively. Moreover, a representative Co‐SAM‐modified device retains 97% of its initial efficiency after 1856 h of maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and Co‐SAM‐modified devices retain 92.36% of their initial efficiency after 2408 h of continuous aging at 65°C (ISOS‐D‐2).

title: Toward a Visible‐Range Helicity Filter: Panchromatic Magnetic Circular Dichroism via 4f‐Orbital‐Based Charge Transfer in a Cerium(IV) Complex
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)‐based light‐helicity filters provide a material‐based approach to controlling the helicity of light. However, helicity control across the entire visible spectrum using a single molecular species has not yet been demonstrated. Herein, we report a tetravalent cerium (Ce(IV)) complex exhibiting panchromatic MCD properties originating from 4f‐orbital‐based ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions. A Ce(IV) complex containing four electron‐donating anionic diethyldithiocarbamate ligands was synthesized. This complex exhibits panchromatic light absorption with both positive (520–780 nm) and negative (380–520 nm) MCD signals. Relativistic time‐dependent density functional theory (TD‐DFT) calculations reveal that this panchromatic light absorption originates from multiple LMCT transitions. The strong spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) associated with the Ce(IV) 4f orbitals facilitates the mixing of singlet and triplet LMCT excited states, enabling panchromatic light absorption. The 4f‐orbital‐based transition properties also contribute to effective MCD signals governed by the Faraday
                    B
                    ‐term. These findings highlight the potential of panchromatic MCD in a Ce(IV) complex as a promising approach toward the development of visible‐range light‐helicity filters.

title: Anion‐Anchoring, Anti‐Swelling Polymer Interphase Enables Durable Lithium Metal Anodes in Localized High‐Concentration Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) can improve the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries by promoting anion‐rich solvation structures that favor the formation of inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). However, their favorable interfacial chemistry is not self‐sustaining because the native SEI is heterogeneous and prone to repeated rupture during Li plating/stripping, thus progressively depleting active Li and electrolyte. Polymeric artificial SEIs have emerged as a complementary strategy for interfacial stabilization, but their effectiveness in LHCEs is limited by an inherent conflict: the polar functional groups that coordinate ions also coordinate solvents, causing polymer swelling, dissolution, and disruption of anion‐rich solvation structures. Here, we develop an anion‐anchoring and anti‐swelling artificial SEI (AS–SEI) by integrating imidazolium cations with long aliphatic side chains. Imidazolium cations enable anion anchoring to sustain the LHCE‐favored anion‐rich environment at the interface, while long aliphatic chains provide anti‐swelling behavior that protects anchoring sites from competitive solvation. Consequently, AS‐SEI exhibits a high Young's modulus (5.0–10.5 GPa) and a high Li
                    +
                    transference number (0.94), while promoting the formation of LiF/Li
                    2
                    O‐rich SEIs. Li||Cu cells achieve 480 cycles with 99.5% average Coulombic efficiency, while Li||NCM811 cells deliver ∼900 cycles with 80% capacity retention (a nearly threefold improvement), with the strategy remaining effective across ether‐, ester‐, and sulfone‐based LHCEs.

title: Interfacial State‐Perturbed Triplet Energy Transfer in Dye‐Sensitized Upconversion Nanoparticles for Early HIV Diagnosis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Early diagnosis of HIV infection is pivotal for curbing AIDS progression and enabling timely therapeutic interventions. However, current immunoassays remain constrained by inadequate sensitivity for detecting trace levels of the HIV‐1 p24 antigen during the seroconversion window period. In this study, we discover that subtle perturbations in the interfacial binding state of a carboxylated near‐infrared dye, Cypate, on sub‐7 nm NaGdF
                    4
                    :Yb
                    3+
                    /Er
                    3+
                    upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) dramatically modulate triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a remarkable upconversion luminescence (UCL) response with a signal‐to‐background ratio as high as 375. By leveraging this interfacial state‐perturbed TET as a signal transduction model, we further develop a TET‐sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET‐ULISA) for HIV‐1 p24 antigen detection. In this platform, the target p24 triggers alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to generate phosphate ions, which competitively displace Cypate from the UCNP surface, disrupting TET and producing a dramatic UCL response. The resulting TET‐ULISA exhibits high sensitivity for p24 antigen with a limit of detection as low as 112 fg mL
                    −1

title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: N‐ Alkyl pyrazoles are common motifs in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their preparation as single regioisomers is often hampered by poor regioselectivity in the direct alkylation of NH‐pyrazoles. Here we report a skeletal‐editing strategy that converts readily available pyridines into regiodefined N‐ alkyl pyrazoles through selective two‐carbon deletion. The N‐ substituent is installed before pyrazole formation and retained through amine‐mediated Zincke‐type ring opening, acid‐promoted cyclization, and retro‐Mannich extrusion of a two‐carbon enamine, fixing the pyrazole regiochemistry at the precursor stage. The sequence contracts the C 5 N pyridine framework into a C 3 N 2 pyrazole, transferring the ring nitrogen, three carbon atoms, and their substitution pattern directly onto the product. The method accommodates diverse pyridine scaffolds and N‐ alkyl groups and enables the skeletal remodeling of structurally complex molecules, transforming a problematic regioselective N‐ alkylation into a programmable precursor‐design strategy.

title: Overriding Polarity Mismatch in Radical Difunctionalization of 1,3‐Dienes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The difunctionalization of conjugated dienes poses a significant challenge in controlling regio‐ and stereoselectivity due to the presence of two conjugated double bonds. Conventional radical addition reactions adhere to the polarity‐matching principle, wherein nucleophilic alkyl radicals preferentially attack the electrophilic C4 position of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes. Consequently, the polarity‐mismatched C1‐selective addition has remained unexplored. Herein, we report a three‐component 1,4‐dicarbofunctionalization of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes with
                    α
                    ‐aminoalkyl radicals and alkyl bromides via dual nickel/photoredox catalysis. This protocol overcomes the inherent polarity‐mismatching effect, achieving unprecedented C1‐selective addition with complete 1,4‐regioselectivity and excellent
                    E
                    ‐stereoselectivity. The reaction provides efficient access to structurally diverse
                    β
                    ‐amino acid derivatives, featuring broad substrate compatibility and promising utility in the derivatization of complex molecules. Combined mechanistic investigations and DFT calculations reveal that both radical addition and C–C reductive elimination govern the regio‐ and stereoselectivity. Notably, a significant hyperconjugative interaction between the forming C–C bond and the carbonyl group of the 1,3‐diene in the transition state plays a pivotal role in directing the radical addition to the polarity‐mismatched C1 position.

title: An Artificial Phosphoinositide Phosphatase Inhibiting Pyroptosis Cascade for Sepsis Treatment
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sepsis mortality remains largely driven by dysregulated pyroptosis, where gasdermin D (GSDMD) pores release lethal cytokines via phosphoinositide (PIP)‐mediated membrane recruitment. To disrupt this process, we engineer terbium‐doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) with sublattice‐induced oxygen vacancies and optimized Ce
                    3+
                    /Ce
                    4+
                    ratios, functioning as artificial phosphatases that achieve > 20‐fold enhanced dephosphorylation activity against the model substrate (
                    para
                    ‐nitrophenyl phosphate) versus pristine nanoparticles. Mechanistically, TCNs dephosphorylate PIPs at the plasma membrane, disrupting the canonical pyroptosis cascade by simultaneously interfering with inflammasome activation and the N‐terminal domain of GSDMD (GSDMD‐NT) oligomerization, ultimately inhibiting lytic pore formation. This
                    pan‐
                    PIP dephosphorylation approach overcomes the limitations of natural phosphatases by enabling efficient lipid dephosphorylation and preventing GSDMD membrane localization. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that TCNs significantly reduce pro‐inflammatory cytokine release and improve survival rates in a murine model of endotoxemic sepsis. This work establishes nanoparticle‐mediated PIP modulation as a potential strategy for sepsis immunotherapy, rebalancing immune homeostasis through precision pyroptosis attenuation.

title: Photocatalytic PVDF Degradation Coupled With Catalytic Targeted Li Replenishment Toward Low‐Energy Repair of Spent LiFePO4 Electrodes

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Directly repair is recognized as a promising route for recycling spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP), but it is challenged by uneven Li supplementation and high energy input. Herein, we propose a photocatalytic strategy for PVDF degradation coupled with targeted Li replenishment toward low‐energy repair of spent LFP materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in‐situ characterizations, TiO

Meanwhile, the photogenerated electrons accumulated on TiO
                    2

                    2+

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Traditional industrial routes for
                    N,N

Electrosynthesis of DMF has emerged as a sustainable alternative; however, this pathway still faces the challenges of low activity and poor selectivity.                     intermediate and *CHO intermediates derived from both methanol and the self‐decomposition of DMA. Furthermore, we find that the introduction of methanol provides a sufficient supply of *CHO intermediates, thereby further enhancing the selectivity of DMF synthesis compared with using DMA as the sole substrate. This work not only identifies the origin of the *CHO donor and its pivotal function in DMF electrosynthesis but also provides a foundation for designing multicomponent synergistic catalysts for advanced electrosynthesis.

title: Supramolecular Iron(II)‐Anchored Porphyrin Glycoassemblies Enable Galectin‐Targeted Photodynamic Therapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on photosensitizers that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon light irradiation to trigger cytotoxic effects in target tissues. Porphyrins are among the most widely used PDT photosensitizers due to their strong visible‐light absorption and efficient ROS generation, although their broad application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation, and limited selectivity. Here, Fe(II)‐anchored porphyrin nanocages displaying peripheral lactose residues were prepared by coordination‐driven subcomponent self‐assembly to combine photodynamic activity with multivalent glycan presentation. The resulting cubic Fe
                    8
                    L
                    6
                    architectures were characterized by NMR spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and transmission electron microscopy. The zinc‐metalated porphyrin nanoassembly, [
                    1‐Zn
                    ][BF
                    4
                    ]
                    16
                    , generated both singlet oxygen and superoxide upon red‐light irradiation, providing access to multiple ROS pathways. Isothermal titration calorimetry revealed high‐affinity binding to galectin‐3 (
                    K
                    d
                     = 2.65 ± 0.26 µM), a lectin commonly upregulated in epithelial cancers. A549 cells treated with [
                    1‐Zn
                    ][BF
                    4
                    ]
                    16
                    exhibited potent light‐induced cytotoxicity with negligible dark toxicity, with a phototoxicity index (PI) of 55, while pre‐treatment with lactose or thiodigalactose was protective against [
                    1‐Zn
                    ][BF
                    4
                    ]
                    16
                    toxicity. These results demonstrate that coordination‐driven self‐assembly provides an effective strategy for integrating multivalent lectin recognition and photodynamic activity within a single nanoscale architecture.

title: Single‐Vesicle Membrane Order‐Resolved Super‐Resolution Imaging Reveals Cholesterol Enrichment and Its Functional Role in Extracellular Vesicle Uptake
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are heterogeneous in membrane composition, yet conventional lipid analysis cannot resolve individual vesicles. Here we develop membrane order‐resolved, spectrally encoded super‐resolution imaging to simultaneously quantify membrane order and size at the single‐EV level. Combining Nile Red single‐molecule spectroscopy with localization microscopy achieves ∼30 nm resolution and reveals pronounced vesicle‐to‐vesicle heterogeneity. Using defined liposomes, cholesterol enrichment, and pharmacological inhibition, we establish membrane order as a sensitive surrogate for relative cholesterol content in individual EVs. Application to EVs from breast, gastric, and oral cell lines reveals cell‐type‐ and tissue‐dependent differences. Most cancer‐cell‐derived EVs show higher membrane order and higher inferred cholesterol than non‐tumor counterparts, although MDA‐MB‐231 EVs are an exception. Functional assays demonstrate that increasing EV membrane cholesterol enhances cellular uptake and shifts internalization from clathrin‐mediated to non‐clathrin‐mediated pathways. These findings identify cholesterol enrichment as a frequent feature of cancer‐cell‐derived EVs and link membrane composition to uptake efficiency and pathway selection. This work provides a single‐EV analytical platform and new insight into how membrane lipid heterogeneity regulates EV‐mediated intercellular communication.

title: Revealing Oxidation‐State‐Dependent Selectivity in Urea Electrosynthesis Over Stabilized Co/CoOx Surfaces
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic upgrading of CO
                    2
                    and nitrogen wastes offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, yet its selectivity is limited by competing parallel reactions and operando catalyst reconstruction. Here, using cobalt‐based model catalysts, we demonstrate that product partitioning among competing pathways can be selectively directed by metallic and oxidized cobalt phases. By introducing oxophilic Cr
                    3+
                    to retard cathodic over‐reduction of cobalt oxides, we stabilize a non‐equilibrium Co/CoO
                    
                      x

                      x

                    −1
                    g
                    cat
                    −1
                    under pressurized CO
                    2
                    at −0.3 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support a proposed oxidation‐state‐dependent relay mechanism in which metallic Co favors CO
                    2

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Narrowband Organic Ultralong Afterglow Through Efficient Two‐Photon Ionization
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic ultralong afterglow (OUA) materials are exclusively constrained by their reliance on host–guest exciplexes, which inherently suffer from spectral broadening and limited color tunability. Here we demonstrate an effective strategy to achieve narrowband OUA by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two‐photon ionization (TPI). Through engineering multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) guests, we achieve full‐color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours, which are comparable to commercial inorganic afterglow materials. The rigid planar molecular architecture of MR‐TADF not only promotes TPI but also reinforces host–guest interactions, thus fostering efficient charge separation to boost OUA properties. The intrinsic OUA can also be achieved based on fluorophore and metal–organic complex guests with planar molecular skeletons. The resultant materials enable promising applications in spectrally pure emergency afterglow lighting and sophisticated afterglow organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). The afterglow OLEDs exhibit a maximum luminance of 26481 cd/m
                    2
                    , an external quantum efficiency of 8.7%, and record‐breaking ultralong electroluminescence afterglow lasting over 15 minutes. Our findings establish a valuable design principle for modulating charge migration and exciton transitions towards developing next‐generation OUA materials.

title: Built‐in Electric Field Modulating Interfacial Charge Dynamics in V2AlC‐Derived Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterostructures for Broadband Microwave Absorption
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The tailored design of magnetic‐dielectric heterostructures offers considerable potential for high‐performance electromagnetic wave absorption, yet achieving efficient interfacial charge separation remains challenging. Herein, we constructed VC/FeCoNi/Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    heterostructures with built‐in electric fields (BIEFs) via the topological structural transformation of V
                    2
                    AlC in Lewis acidic molten salts. This transformation involves the redox‐potential‐driven substitution by Fe/Co/Ni cations, leading to in situ alloying within the VC interlayers to balance the electromagnetic parameters. Theoretical calculations reveal that the work‐function difference drives directional interfacial charge redistribution, as evidenced by experimental observations of charge transfer and surface‐potential differences. This charge redistribution reconstructs the local electronic states, leading to interfacial orbital hybridization and establishing BIEFs at the heterointerfaces. Atomic vacancies and lattice distortions generated during etching, coupled with the BIEFs, enhance interfacial and defect‐induced polarization. Consequently, the optimized composite achieves a wide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.72 GHz (at 1.7 mm) and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB (at 2.8 mm). This BIEF‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy offers a viable route for designing high‐performance broadband microwave absorbers.

title: Molecular Crystal Phase Transformation via Nonclassical Pathways: Surfactant‐Based Kinetic Control of Metastable Amorphous Intermediates
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Molecular crystals serve as essential components in a wide range of functional products, yet their performance is often compromised by unpredictable phase transformations, particularly in aqueous environments. Although nonclassical, multistage pathways are frequently proposed for such transitions, the specific role of transient intermediates remains poorly understood. Here, we employ in situ atomic force microscopy and high‐resolution transmission electron microscopy to elucidate a nonclassical transformation pathway in the model molecular crystal piroxicam that proceeds via metastable intermediates. These intermediates serve as amorphous precursors that undergo densification prior to crystallization, facilitating a rapid transition from the anhydrate to a less soluble hydrate phase. The onset and kinetics of this transformation are tunable through the use of cationic surfactants with varying alkyl‐chain lengths. Longer‐chain surfactants cooperatively adsorb onto both dissolving crystal facets and nanodroplets in solution, creating a dense interfacial barrier that delays precursor formation and subsequent crystallization. This work presents a strategy to manipulate phase transformation pathways in molecular crystals by targeting the metastable intermediates via tailored additive‐interface interactions, enabling the predictive design of advanced materials with controlled phase behavior and enhanced performance reliability.

title: Tailoring the Na+ Transport Microenvironment With an Anion‐Capturing Interface Enables Low‐Temperature, Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Na
                    +
                    desolvation and diffusion across the solid‐electrolyte interface (SEI) are two bottlenecks to fast charging at low temperatures in hard‐carbon sodium‐ion batteries. Here, we design an anion‐capturing interface that provides a customized interfacial environment to enhance interfacial dynamics at low temperatures. We demonstrate that phosphate can promote the formation of a homogeneous inorganic SEI by inducing anion enrichment near the inner Helmholtz plane. The phosphorus‐rich interface exhibits multiple benefits, including the formation of a built‐in electric field and a reduced energy barrier for Na
                    +
                    interphase diffusion. The hard carbon–phosphate interface (NP‐HC) anode maintains a capacity of 183.6 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.5 A g
                    −1
                    (−30°C). The pouch cell utilizing the NP‐HC anode achieves a 90.2% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at a 2 C rate. Even so, NP‐HC pouch cells can operate stably even at temperatures as low as −40°C, indicating their potential to enhance the performance of sodium‐ion batteries under harsh conditions.

title: A General Strategy to Identify Impurity‐Activated Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Synthetic Triarylamines
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Distinguishing intrinsic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) from impurity‐derived emission remains challenging in organic luminescent materials, particularly when trace emissive species evade routine characterization. Herein, we establish a diagnostic framework for identifying impurity‐activated RTP in synthetic triarylamines through route‐, fraction‐, and purification‐dependent validation, impurity reconstitution, and theoretical analysis. Using TPA, TPAO, and related heteroatom‐engineered triarylamines as representative systems, we show that nominally identical samples can exhibit different RTP behaviors depending on synthetic history and purification extent, despite appearing chemically indistinguishable by conventional analyses. Progressive purification induces blue‐shifted and narrowed emissions and ultimately eliminates afterglow, revealing hidden emissive species. Structural analyses identify trace C–H arylation byproducts generated during metal‐catalyzed coupling reactions as a representative class of RTP‐active impurities. Reintroduction of independently synthesized impurity candidates into rigorously purified hosts restores phosphorescence, providing direct functional evidence that synthesis‐derived byproducts can activate RTP. Theoretical calculations further show that these impurities possess lower‐lying triplet states and act as triplet‐energy traps. Extension of the workflow to related synthetic triarylamines reproduces purification‐dependent RTP loss and impurity‐enabled recovery, supporting the applicability of this strategy across the triarylamine systems examined here and establishing synthetic history and purification as critical variables in assigning the origin of organic RTP.

title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Sharpless Asymmetric Dihydroxylation With Expanded Substrate Compatibility
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is an established transformation in organic synthesis for the preparation of chiral vicinal diols. However, conventional biphasic solution‐based conditions (typically water/
                    t‐
                    BuOH) require long reaction times (up to ∼48 h) and large amounts of solvent. Moreover, they often exhibit limited substrate scope due to low solubility of the substrates and functional‐group incompatibility. Herein, we report the first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation, which affords the desired diols with excellent enantioselectivity, comparable to that of conventional methods. Notably, most substrates are fully converted within 30 min without the need for large quantities of solvent. Moreover, the mechanochemical conditions enable efficient reactions of substrates that are challenging to convert under solution‐based conditions, including poorly soluble, base‐sensitive, and catalyst‐coordinating compounds. The practical utility of this protocol is further demonstrated by the efficient dihydroxylation of an intermediate of a natural product and a gram‐scale synthesis.

title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  A paired electrochemical synthetic strategy for the upcycling of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is reported, enabling simultaneous cathodic dechlorination of the polymer backbone and anodic formation of cyclic halo acetals (CHAs) as monomer precursors. The process channels liberated chloride into cyclic acetal structures, which are converted into cyclic ketene acetals and subsequently polymerized via radical ring‐opening polymerization (rROP) to access degradable polyester and poly(amino ester) materials. Electrochemical cyclization unlocks the synthesis of previously unavailable nitrogen‐containing cyclic ketene acetal monomers in remarkably high yields. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal a pronounced heteroatom effect on cyclization efficiency, attributed to conformational preorganization induced by an increasing gauche effect upon ether and amide incorporation. A nitrogen‐containing ketene acetal monomer was polymerized and copolymerized with established ketene acetals, affording new functional, biodegradable polymer materials. Successful copolymerization with methyl acrylate demonstrates the incorporation of hydrolysable moieties into otherwise persistent olefinic materials. Importantly, cathodic PVC dechlorination proceeds independently of the anodic transformation, highlighting the broad applicability of this paired‐electrolysis strategy in an undivided cell. Overall, this work establishes a versatile electrochemical PVC recycling process while simultaneously generating previously inaccessible monomer building blocks for biodegradable polymer synthesis.

title: Hofmeister Engineering Enables High‐Voltage Aqueous All‐Organic Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous all‐organic batteries (AOBs) offer a safe and sustainable alternative for electrochemical energy storage, yet their energy density is constrained by the limited availability of organic redox couples with high‐working voltages. Here we develop a versatile redox couple by pairing a 3,4,9,10‐perylenetetracarboxylic diimide (PTCDI) anode with a quaternary‐ammonium bromine cathode, enabling an initial discharge voltage of up to 2.0 V through reversible two‐electron bromine conversion (Br
                    −
                    /Br
                    0
                    /Br
                    +
                    ). This battery chemistry is compatible with diverse charge carriers, including Li
                    +
                    , Na
                    +
                    , K
                    +
                    , NH
                    4
                    +
                    , Ca
                    2+
                    , and Mg
                    2+
                    . We further reveal that electrolyte ions exert distinct effects on electrode reactions: Cations primarily regulate reaction kinetics, whereas anions govern both reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect. Kosmotropic anions suppress polybromide dissolution and improve reversibility, but retard electrode kinetics, while chaotropic anions facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of active‐material retention. Guided by this mechanistic insight, a hybrid kosmotropic/chaotropic electrolyte balances these competing effects. The optimized one‐electron configuration retains 83.1% of its capacity after 12 000 cycles, while the two‐electron configuration delivers an energy density of approximately 107 Wh kg
                    −1
                    based on the combined electrode active‐material mass. High areal capacities exceeding 4 mAh cm
                    −2
                    further demonstrate its practical potential. This work establishes electrolyte solvation engineering as an effective strategy for high‐energy AOBs.

title: MitoDART: Mitochondria‐Targeted Intracellular DNA Assembly for Selective Mitochondrial Interference and Early Molecular Response Monitoring
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Rational modulation of mitochondrial functions to reprogram cellular behavior and fate has emerged as a promising therapeutic paradigm. However, it is still challenging to achieve cell‐selective mitochondrial interference with in situ monitoring of early molecular responses. In this study, we report a
                    mito
                    chondria‐targeted dual‐biomarker‐activated intracellular
                    D
                    NA
                    a
                    ssembly for mitochondrial
                    r
                    egulation and
                    t
                    racking (Mito‐DART), which enables cell‐selective interference of mitochondria and in situ biosensing for early assessment of molecular responses. Based on the AND logic responsive to two tumor biomarkers, apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) and microRNAs, Mito‐DART is specifically activated in tumor cells and undergoes hybridization chain reaction (HCR)‐driven DNA assembly, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis‐associated cellular responses. More importantly, Mito‐DART enables in situ monitoring of cytochrome c (Cyt c) release, an early molecular marker of mitochondria‐mediated apoptosis, within 1 h following mitochondrial disruption, providing an early molecular readout of mitochondria‐mediated apoptotic signaling that complements conventional tissue‐level endpoint assessments. Overall, this design provides a programmable framework for biomarker‐gated mitochondrial intervention that combines selective activation with built‐in assessment of downstream molecular responses.

title: Novel Fluorinated Amino‐Ester Electrolyte With Host–Guest Solvation Enables High‐Voltage and Thermally Safe Lithium–Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium–metal batteries (LMBs) face critical bottlenecks to high energy density, long cycle life, and thermal safety, mainly due to insufficient oxidation stability and thermal tolerance of solvation structures in conventional carbonate/ether electrolytes. In this work, we develop a host–guest solvation structure via a molecular fluorination strategy based on a tertiary amine‐ester scaffold functionalized with trifluoroethyl (CF

The distinct polarity contrast between TFE and HFS delivers functional complementarity: TFE, with strong Lewis basicity, promotes lithium‐salt dissociation, while highly fluorinated HFS, with weak solvation ability, accelerates interfacial reduction kinetics through a delocalized charge‐transfer mechanism, forming a LiF/Li

title: Hole Mobility Synchronizes Carbon Oxidation and Nitrate Reduction to Switch Photocatalytic Selectivity between Ammonia and Urea
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocatalytic conversion of nitrate and renewable carbon feedstocks offers a sustainable route to nitrogen chemicals but remains constrained by mismatched oxidation–reduction kinetics and inefficient C–N coupling. Here, we identify hole mobility as a decisive kinetic regulator that governs nitrate photoreduction selectivity by synchronizing carbon activation and nitrogen reduction pathways. By introducing cadmium vacancies into single‐atom Cu‐anchored CdS, we substantially reduce effective hole mass and accelerate hole transport, enabling oxidative C–C cleavage of biomass‐derived oxalic‐acid to generate reactive *COOH. Concurrently, hole mobility‐induced electron localization at Cu stabilizes nitrate‐derived *NH
                    2
                    , promoting selective *NH
                    2
                    ‐*COOH coupling while suppressing deep protonation to ammonia. Accordingly, Cu/CdS‐V
                    Cd
                    achieves a record urea yield of 1024 µmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with >99% selectivity, approximately fourteen times higher than state‐of‐the‐art nitrate‐based photocatalysts. In contrast, vacancy‐free Cu/CdS with low hole mobility fails to activate carbon feedstock and instead produces ammonia with >99% selectivity. In‐situ spectroscopy and density functional theory reveal that enhanced hole mobility accelerates oxalic‐acid oxidation, strengthens *NH
                    2
                    adsorption, and lowers the free‐energy barrier for C–N coupling to enable selective urea formation. These findings establish charge‐carrier mobility, rather than isolated active‐site activity, as a governing principle for artificial photosynthesis, offering a general strategy for selective multi‐reactant photocatalytic transformations.

title: Pulse‐Programmable Electrostatic Memory Using Ultrathin Hexagonal Boron Nitride
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Non‐volatile memory elements that enable multifunctionality and seamless integration with emerging quantum materials are of increasing interest for next‐generation electronic systems. In van der Waals heterostructures, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is widely employed as an inert substrate, encapsulation layer, and gate dielectric. Here we show that ultrathin (∼1.2 nm) hBN can also function as an active, pulse‐programmable electrostatic medium, enabling non‐volatile resistive memory with tunable resistance states in a multi‐terminal device architecture without dedicated gate or floating‐gate elements. Under millisecond current pulses, devices exhibit robust polarity‐dependent hysteresis in both transverse and longitudinal resistance, with programmed states exhibiting long retention times up to room temperature. The switching amplitude is strongly enhanced near the charge‐neutrality regime and vanishes in control devices without hBN, establishing ultrathin hBN as the essential functional element. We attribute this behavior to field‐assisted charge injection and trapping in hBN and near its interfaces, generating metastable electret‐like states that modify the local electrostatic potential landscape and thereby reconfigure electronic transport in the underlying channel. Our results identify few‐layer hBN as an active dielectric platform for non‐volatile memory and reveal a route toward electrostatically programmable transport functionalities in van der Waals systems.

title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras-driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c-MYC-driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c-MYC-driven PLCs, Pten-deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten-deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8+ T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs

abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude (
                    M
                    ) <3] are commonly modeled as simple circular ruptures, leaving the fine-scale spatial attributes of rupture dynamics unresolved. We used near-source distributed acoustic sensing to image the millisecond-scale rupture of an
                    M
                    2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California’s Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the
                    M
                    2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude (
                    M
                    w
                    ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four
                    M
                    w
                    7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

title: Rebuilding science’s social contract with the public
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Much has been written about how the social contract between science and society in the United States is in crisis. According to its terms, research will yield broad economic, health, and security benefits to the very public that funds it. But this relationship depends on public trust in science, its systems, and the scientists themselves, and therein lies the problem. Beyond making discoveries and publishing results, scientists shape their own culture, and that is where some changes may be the key to rebuilding public trust.

title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.
